payload.description:
`make app` in demo/Makefile says "pre-build the standalone runner (do this first; it is the slow one)" but runs:

    cd muster-ui && nix build 'path:.#default' --out-link .run/app

That is `packages.default`. `make run` launches with `nix run 'path:.'`, which is `apps.default`. Resolved on 2026-08-13, they are different derivations:

    packages.default      -> /nix/store/03n3y6r187...-logos-muster_ui-module
    apps.default.program  -> /nix/store/q4gpjhnqal...-run-logos-standalone-ui/bin/run-logos-standalone-ui
    .run/app symlink      -> /nix/store/03n3y6r187...-logos-muster_ui-module

So `make app` out-links the .lgx module and returns in seconds, then `make alice` starts building the standalone runner -- which pulls lez_core and with it the RISC Zero proving stack from Rust source. Measured: 827 cargo-package derivations and still going at 36 minutes. The target's whole purpose is defeated, and its name (.run/app) points at something that is not the app.

Compounding it: nix defaults to max-jobs = 1 and there is no nix.conf here setting otherwise, so that build runs strictly serially -- 41 derivations/min at load 2.5 on a 16-core machine. Relaunching with NIX_CONFIG='max-jobs = 8' took it to roughly 110/min.

Fix, two parts:
1. Point `make app` at the runner. The flake already demonstrates the trick at flake.nix:81-82 -- `packages.exchange` interpolates `base.apps.${system}.default.program`, so building it warms the runner into the store. Either reuse that or expose a `packages.runner` for the standalone app derivation and out-link that.
2. Have the demo pass --max-jobs (or document it in RUNBOOK.md), so a first launch on a cold store is not an hour of one-at-a-time crate builds.

Found while launching two peers to confirm the LEZ retraction work (exo-fb8). Not related to that change -- it is pre-existing.
payload.title: make app does not pre-build the runner it claims to

payload.description:
Observed in the two-peer run on 2026-08-13 (alice -> bob, credited successfully).

A shielded payee has no address to watch, so there is nothing to subscribe to -- the money is found by scanning with the viewing key. That part is the design, not a defect (see GAPS.md 4b). What is missing is that nothing in the app performs that scan on the payee's behalf.

Evidence: bob's chat_ui log after 10:20 contains nothing but health probes. He made no transfer, so no settleAfterTransfer runs for him, and there is no periodic wallet poll anywhere in the backend -- the only repeating timer is m_healthProbe (ChatBackend.cpp:221). His balance moved only when a human pressed Refresh.

The trigger should be the conversation, which is where the news already arrives. The sender posts a send-receipt card, and the payee's client already parses it: ChatBackendJourney.cpp:151 and ChatBackendIntent.cpp:145 both branch on type == "send-receipt" to fold it into the journey. Nothing on that path touches the wallet. Proposed: when an inbound send-receipt names a rail whose destination is a holding this wallet owns, kick refreshBalances() -- or better, the settleAfterTransfer poll loop, since the payee faces the same 'accepted but not yet visible' lag the sender does.

Honesty constraint, which is why this is not just 'call refresh': a receipt is authenticated in the room but the zone checks none of it (see the authorization claim in VisibilityClaims.qml). The receipt may therefore trigger a *scan*, because a scan only looks -- but the UI must never render 'you were paid' on the receipt's word. It must show what the scan actually found, and say nothing if the scan found nothing yet.

Fallback if the automatic trigger is deferred: a visible affordance on the private holding telling the payee that money is found by scanning and that Refresh is how they do it. Right now a payee who was told 'I sent it' sees an unchanged balance and no explanation, which is indistinguishable from the payment having failed -- the same confusion that produced the withdrawn report in exo-fb8.

Not a regression from exo-fb8; it is a gap that work revealed. Consider disclosing it in GAPS.md and the payment claim once the behaviour is decided.
payload.title: A payee discovers a shielded payment only by pressing Refresh

criteria:

    pins: provenance is structurally in the signed bytes, not attached alongside

authoring: every oracle was LLM-proposed; the human critiqued and confirmed, and hand-wrote none.

DEVIATIONS FROM SKILL ACCEPTANCE — recorded rather than papered over:
  1. No correct->regenerate round occurred. The skill considers a discussion complete only
     with at least one demonstrated round where the first proposal was weak. All five were
     confirmed as first proposed. A weak proposal was not manufactured to satisfy the

  2. Executor gap, decided deliberately: s2/s3/s4 are model_check, whose executor is not

     conserving a count of provenance entries is the cancellation hole the skill doc warns

     green). Assurance for s2/s3/s4 is DECLARED, NOT DISCHARGED until the executor lands.
  3. No handoff yaml: this repo runs no exophial dispatch (see
     docs/labbook/exophial-hooks-without-dispatch.md), so there is no session handoff dir.

Follow-on: CLAUDE.md invariant 10 drafted in the same pass, citing this spec.
spec: contracts/specs/derived-exo-3a1.spec.json

REVISION (session 700cc87e) — spec regenerated at 6 spans

Operator challenge: "no identity in the trail" is over-strict from a disclosure
standpoint. Anyone in a conversation can disclose anything they have access to;
what matters is that anyone OUTSIDE the conversation cannot see.

Adjudicated against the sources rather than accepted or rejected wholesale:

  RIGHT, and a real defect in v1. FS-7 is conditional and scoped — "For
  ANONYMOUS-MEMBERSHIP drivers... WITHIN the client" — and derived-exo-f60 opens
  "When a driver declares an anonymous membership model". v1 s4 was written
  UNCONDITIONALLY ("never contains signer identity for any input class"),
  over-applying f60 past its own scope and gutting the trail in a named
  conversation, where "a peer message at log position 42" withholds a name every
  participant already holds.

  NOT RIGHT for anonymous drivers. There the participants cannot disclose what
  they do not have — that is what the driver is for — so recording identity would
  hand insiders precisely what f60 exists to withhold. The disclosure argument
  does not reach that case.

  s4 RESCOPED, not dropped: conditional on the driver-declared membership model
  (invariant 6 — driver-described, never core-hardcoded). The stepper now
  enumerates model x signer-assignment and asserts a DIFFERENT thing per branch,
  which is what stops the named branch passing vacuously: anonymous => record
  invariant under permutation; named => record covaries exactly, so the recorded
  account is the actual contributor rather than an arbitrary or stale one.

  GAP THE CHALLENGE EXPOSED. v1 had NO outsider clause at all — s1..s5 covered
  contents and derivation, nothing covered who can read it. Worse, s5 has a hole
  the challenge falls straight through: a provenance file written IN THE CLEAR
  beside the log satisfies cold-start replay perfectly while handing a keyless
  actor the whole lineage. New s6 pins the boundary: confined to the conversation,
  scoped to the membership epoch of the entries it describes, unreconstructable
  without that epoch keys. Also catches a member joining at epoch E+1 rebuilding
  epoch-E provenance — defeating derived-exo-525 through the trail rather than
  through the content.

  s5 deliberately LEFT AS AUTHORED. Its probe still would not catch the clear-text
  side file on its own; s6 catches it directly, so strengthening s5 was declined as
  redundant. Recorded because it is a real limitation of s5 read alone.

APPEND-ONLY TENSION, flagged and ruled on by the operator rather than assumed:
CLAUDE.md says invariant tests are append-only, extend do not weaken. Narrowing s4
is a scope reduction. Judged legitimate because s4 was hours old with no
implementation and no running probe, so nothing depended on it, and the net change
is strengthening — s6 covers a threat previously uncovered. The reasoning is
recorded here BECAUSE it is the reasoning that erodes invariants when used
carelessly.

restatement: revised block approved before either oracle was authored.
oracles: s4 revised and s6 new, both LLM-proposed and human-confirmed.
unchanged: s1, s2, s3, s5.
executor gap unchanged: s2/s3/s4/s6 are model_check, declared not discharged;
only s1 and s5 execute today.

payload.description:
Upstream bug in logos-co/logos-chat-module, pinned at dfe8ccf3 (2026-08-04) in demo/muster-ui/flake.lock. Found 2026-08-14 while designing pre-populated demo state.

SYMPTOM. Every launch of a peer starts with no conversations, and its chat address is different. Measured across three sessions -- alice sees bob as 3096fd24, then 0a91a0ca, then b3f8b3be; bob sees alice as e58fc481, then 36681062, then 55cbb48c. A conversation created and used with messages exchanged, followed by a clean shutdown (chat_module 'shutdown' called, app exit code 0), is gone on relaunch. Reproduced twice.

CAUSE. Persistence is implemented but not used. chat_module_plugin.so contains a full SQLite layer:

    INSERT OR REPLACE INTO conversations (local_convo_id, remote_convo_id, convo_type) VALUES (?1, ?2, ?3)
    SELECT local_convo_id, remote_convo_id, convo_type FROM conversations
    SELECT name, secret_key FROM identity WHERE id = 1
    INSERT OR REPLACE INTO identity (id, name, secret_key) VALUES (1, ?1, ?2)
    CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS ephemeral_keys (...)

plus ratchet_state and skipped_keys tables, and the error string 'host did not assign an instance persistence path; start the host with a session or config dir'. The contract says so too (chat_module.lidl:69): 'Storage lives under the instance directory the host assigns; init fails when the host assigned none.'

But the binary also contains ':memory:', and no named database filename -- the only .db/.sqlite strings are SQLite's own internals (temp.sqlite, vacuum_db.sqlite, anon.db). No database file is created anywhere on the filesystem during a session; a search of the whole home dir over a session window found nothing. chat_module logs 'init: state installed' on every start and logs nothing at shutdown. The connection is opened in memory, so the schema is created fresh each run and discarded at exit.

Inference to flag: ':memory:' in a strings dump is not proof of the connection string in use. But combined with no file on disk, no named db filename, 'state installed' every init, and demonstrably non-surviving identity, the case is strong. Confirming it needs the module source, which we do not have checked out.

NOT CONFIGURABLE. ChatConfig has two optional fields, delivery_preset and log_level. Nothing about storage.

IMPACT ON US.
1. No pre-populated demo state is possible for conversations. Wallet state is ours and persists fine (module_data/chat_module/<instance>/muster-wallet/*.json); the conversation cannot be snapshotted at all, because even restored messages would name addresses that no longer exist.
2. An identity that changes every restart means a peer address shared out of band -- which is what create_conversation consumes -- is only valid for one session.

NEXT. Report upstream with this evidence, the way the LEZ findings went. Ask whether the in-memory open is deliberate for the testnet build or an oversight, and what it would take to point it at the instance persistence path the host already assigns.

Related: exo-d0f, exo-d6d.
payload.title: chat_module opens its store in memory, so identity and conversations die on exit

payload.body:
Retracted the ':memory:' inference while drafting the upstream report. SQLite is statically linked into chat_module_plugin.so (609 sqlite3_ symbols, amalgamation version strings), so ':memory:' is present in any binary bundling SQLite regardless of the connection string in use. It is not evidence of anything.

What survives, and is stronger than what it replaced: the module is launched with --instance-persistence-path and writes its own log into exactly that directory every run, so the path is assigned, exists and is writable — and no database appears there or anywhere else. And the binary contains 'SELECT name, secret_key FROM identity WHERE id = 1', which has no purpose unless identity is meant to be reloaded across runs.

Draft report for the developers: demo/poc/BUG-chat-module-state-not-persisted.md. It is written to be corrected rather than accepted — §3 lists five things we cannot determine from outside, including whether delivery_preset 'logos.test' selects ephemeral storage, which would explain the whole thing.

Answered upstream 2026-08-14. Confirmed, and it is not our bug and not configurable: persistence is not implemented for lambdaAccounts + lambdaChat, all conversations and identities are ephemeral. It was implemented for pairwise conversations and regressed on the pivot to DeMLS; held deliberately until group state is stable, to cut down on forked groups and state desync.

Tracking: logos-messaging/libchat#28. Roadmap: installation management, 2026 chat beta.

None of our five hypotheses was right — not the logos.test preset, not the standalone host, not a build feature, not a derived path. The SQL we found in the binary is residue of the pairwise implementation that regressed: the tables are compiled in, nothing calls them under DeMLS.

Method note worth keeping: reading capability out of a shipped binary tells you what the code once did, not what it currently does. A dead path and a live one look identical in a strings dump.

Settles the demo-state design: the wallet can be pre-populated, the conversation never can, until libchat#28 lands. Response recorded in demo/poc/BUG-chat-module-state-not-persisted.md section 6; the false 'survives a restart' claim in demo/CLAUDE.md is corrected.

payload.description:
Reported from use, 2026-08-14: starting the 'pay someone' flow posts an address-request card in the sender's own thread as though the ask happened, but the receiver is never asked.

MECHANISM. ChatBackend.cpp:753 (and :756 for the 'request' verb) fires requestAddress(convoId) from applyConversationCreated, as soon as the *local* conversation exists. But create_conversation only sends the cryptographic invite -- the peer has not joined the MLS group yet. The card is therefore sent into a group of one: chat_module accepts it, emits message_sent, applyMessageSent renders it locally, and the sender sees 'Asked for an address' with nothing having been asked.

This is not a delivery delay. The message is encrypted to an MLS epoch the peer was never a member of, so it cannot be read by them once they join either. Store-node catchup cannot help.

Our own doctest already works around exactly this, at doctests/exchange/run-exchange.mjs:132: 'create_conversation sends only the cryptographic invite; wait until Alice has joined (her conversation list shows it) before Bob's first message, so the message reaches her subscribed thread rather than racing ahead of her join'. It waits by watching the RECEIVER. The app cannot do that.

WHY THERE IS NO EASY FIX. The sender has no signal that the peer joined a direct conversation:
- GroupMember.pending is documented as never set for a direct conversation -- chat_module.lidl:104, 'A direct conversation reports both participants and never a pending one'. So the roster looks complete from the instant it is created.
- delivery_state_changed(delivery_state, detail) is transport-wide -- it is the Status record's field, alongside convo_count -- not a per-message receipt. There is no way to learn whether a given message landed.
- members_changed may or may not fire for a direct conversation when the peer commits. NOT VERIFIED; needs a live two-peer run to establish, and it is the one thing that could make a clean fix possible.

OPTIONS, none obviously right:
1. Hold the card until there is evidence the conversation is two-way, and say so on screen ('waiting for them to join') rather than sending into the void. Honest, and works without a signal, but the wait is unbounded and the demo's first move becomes a spinner.
2. Retry the send on a timer for ~60s. Needs no signal, but the peer may end up with two address requests, and it still cannot confirm.
3. Wait on members_changed, if it fires. Cleanest if it works -- verify first.
4. Do not auto-send at all: land the user in the conversation with the ask ready to send by hand. Least magic, least wrong.

Whichever we pick, the sender's card must stop asserting an ask that did not happen -- that is the part that is actively misleading, and it is the same class of error as a receipt for a payment nobody made.

WORTH REPORTING UPSTREAM regardless: there is no way for a sender to know a direct conversation is ready to carry a message, and no per-message delivery state. Either would make this solvable at the app layer. Related to the notes in poc/BUG-chat-module-state-not-persisted.md.

payload.body: Build half of the spike GREEN on this Fedora box. Cloned logos-module-builder@nim-cdylib-authoring (codegen.nim + nim.link external-lib linking) to ~/Github/logos-co/. 'nix build .#default' and '.#lgx' both exit 0 via cache.nix.logos.co (only ~7 local derivations; rest cached). Codegen detected the full 5-method surface from muster.lidl (health/propose/txhash/approve/status) -> muster_module_plugin.so + muster-module.lgx (888KB at result-lgx/). module/flake.lock now committed-able. Remaining: build logos-liblogos(logoscore)+lgpm via cache and confirm load+health() in host. Note: user is NOT a trusted nix user (trusted-users=root) and logos cache isn't in global nix.conf, so builds need explicit --extra-substituters flags; the workspace _tool-wrapper scripts don't pass them.

LOAD half proven: logoscore loads muster_module in a logos_host subprocess, dispatches health() over Qt Remote Objects, exits 0 ('Method call successful'). Cmd: logoscore -m result-install-portable/modules -l muster_module -c 'muster_module.health()' --quit-on-finish (needs .#install-portable, NOT .#install — the latter keys the manifest 'linux-amd64-dev' which logoscore's default variant resolution rejects; portable keys it 'linux-amd64'). CAVEAT: the return rendered as 'Result: false' not 'ok'. Nim side is correct (musterHealth()="ok"; logos_module_dispatch returns JSON "ok"). The false enters the generic bridge; run also showed capability-token handshake failures (ad-hoc -m pulled a mismatched capability_module from logoscore's built-in store). Untyped --call artifact vs real marshalling drop is unresolved from this path. The P4 UI uses the TYPED client (MusterModule::health()->QString), not --call. Spun exo for the verification.

If real, it blocks P4 (UI reads string returns). Good first exophial dispatch --pinned candidate. Context on pebble exo-1f8.

payload.description: exophial's integrator re-grades oracles in a HERMETIC env whose PATH is a hardcoded allowlist (uv/git/bash/sh/pb/check-jsonschema/pre-commit/claude) + /usr/local/bin:/usr/bin:/bin, scrubbing os.environ (spec_oracle._construct_oracle_child_env, _ORACLE_TOOLCHAIN_BINARIES/_ORACLE_SYSTEM_DIRS). muster's oracles run 'nim r -d:release tests/probes/probe_*.nim'; the host-level probes also link the module staticlib against secp256k1. So the regate FAILS: nim lives in ~/.nix-profile/bin (not a system dir) and -lsecp256k1 isn't on the default linker path (it's in the nix store). This blocks INTEGRATION of every muster nim/C++ dispatch (first hit: exo-526, which was verified-green by hand and landed manually). Two-sided fix: (1) provision nim into the hermetic PATH — e.g. 'sudo ln -s ~/.nix-profile/bin/nim /usr/local/bin/nim', OR make exophial's oracle toolchain extensible (config-declared extra bins); (2) make muster probes self-contain their native libs — pass -L<nix-store secp256k1>/lib from metadata.json nix.packages instead of relying on ambient LIBRARY_PATH. Until closed, muster dispatches complete the worker+verify but park at integrate. Context: exo-526, exo-1f8.

So the ONLY remaining step is provisioning nim into a system dir the hermetic env reads: 'sudo ln -s $(readlink -f $(which nim)) /usr/local/bin/nim'. After that, muster nim/C++ dispatches auto-integrate (no manual land). Proper long-term fix (needs the exophial repo, not checked out here): make the oracle toolchain config-extensible so a repo declares extra bins (nim) rather than relying on a system-dir symlink.

payload.description: The muster-ui module BUILDS (commit c26d1f5) but its view never renders in the standalone runner. Diagnosed decisively: (1) run-logos-standalone-ui loads capability_module + the backend deps (muster_module) then stops — no ui_qml view load, no QML engine start, blank 263-byte window, no onContextReady/health. (2) NOT a muster bug: the module-builder's OWN canonical template ui_example (zero deps) renders an identical blank window. (3) NOT a GL/headless issue: xvfb + QT_QUICK_BACKEND=software/LIBGL_ALWAYS_SOFTWARE=1 don't help. (4) Smoking gun: repeated 'QObject::connect: No such signal ::eventResponse(QString,QVariantList)' from capability_module — a QtRO signal-signature SKEW. mkStandaloneApp bundles the standalone-app's OWN capability_module, built against a different logos-qt-sdk/protocol than the module-builder (nim-cdylib-authoring) used for muster_ui; the mismatch blocks the UI-load handshake so the view never loads. Options to close: (a) align logos-standalone-app <-> module-builder qt-sdk/protocol/capability_module pins (follows across both); (b) render muster-ui in logos-basecamp (present at ~/Github/logos-co/logos-basecamp) which carries its own matching capability_module; (c) logos-qt-mcp if it bundles a matching host. Build-half proven; this blocks the headless UI verification (health()->ok surfacing in the view). Context: the P4 spike, exo-526 (same capability-token warning class appeared in logoscore).

payload.body: MAJOR progress + correction. My original 'capability skew' framing was incomplete. Confirmed: (1) the logos-standalone-app CANNOT render any ui_qml view on this box (universal — the module-builder's own ui_example template blank too; not GL/headless, software render doesn't help). (2) DECISIVE: logos-basecamp (built from ~/Github/logos-co/logos-basecamp, default 'app' pkg) RENDERS its full UI headlessly under xvfb + QT_QUICK_BACKEND=software (32KB screenshot: sidebar, MDI window, 'load a UI plugin by clicking on it'). So headless QtQuick works; the standalone runner was the broken host. (3) muster-ui .#lgx-portable + muster_module .#lgx-portable install cleanly into a basecamp --user-dir via 'lgpm install --file X.lgx --modules-dir <ud>/modules --ui-plugins-dir <ud>/plugins' (dev .#lgx is keyed linux-amd64-dev which lgpm rejects; portable is keyed linux-amd64). (4) BUT basecamp loaded only its embedded set (capability_module, package_manager), NOT the user-installed muster_ui/muster_module: basecamp manages modules through a package-manager REGISTRY (PackageCoordinator: embedded + user modules/plugins dirs) — an installed module is available but must be ENABLED/loaded via the Package Manager to appear. FINAL MILE: use logos-qt-mcp (built as a basecamp pkg: 'logos-qt-mcp'/'mcp-server') to drive basecamp's Package Manager to enable muster_ui, click its sidebar icon, and assert the view shows 'muster_module.health() -> ok'. That is the designed P4 acceptance flow. muster-ui build+install proven; icon+lgx packaging committed (9048496). Retitling this from 'standalone-app skew' to the real story: standalone-app can't render ui_qml here; basecamp is the working host; remaining = qt-mcp enable+assert.

ROOT CAUSE + EXACT FIX (drove the full P4 acceptance to the last ABI step). Progress in basecamp (the version-coherent host): (1) muster-ui BUILDS + baked into basecamp installedDev -> REGISTERED, its 'M' icon appears in the sidebar. (2) logos-qt-mcp harness (basecamp tests/ui-tests.mjs pattern) drives it: app.click('muster_ui') works. (3) basecamp loads muster_module — after two packaging fixes: dev .lgx is keyed linux-amd64-dev (recognized) vs portable linux-amd64 (NOT recognized by the dev core), and the dev muster_module_plugin.so has libsecp256k1.so.5 as NEEDED but its RUNPATH omits secp256k1's dir (build links -lsecp256k1 without -rpath) — dropping libsecp256k1.so.5 into the module dir ($ORIGIN, which IS in the RUNPATH) fixes the load. (4) ui-host spawns + 'loaded plugin muster_ui' — THEN CRASHES: std::bad_alloc, exit 6, during view-module INSTANTIATION (before checkHealth runs). ROOT CAUSE (rev comparison basecamp<->module-builder): logos-view-module-runtime 1fde7d43 vs 3c3735c2 and logos-cpp-sdk 4b66dac0 vs e3744fb8 are SKEWED (qt-sdk c6be61d0 + protocol 03842db5 MATCH). The view-module-runtime is the exact ui-host<->plugin contract; the skew corrupts view-module instantiation -> bad_alloc. EXACT FIX: rebuild muster-ui via the module-builder with logos-view-module-runtime pinned to 1fde7d43bb2d and logos-cpp-sdk to 4b66dac015e4 (basecamp's revs) — an input override in muster/ui/flake.nix (or module-builder), then rebuild the baked-in basecamp + rerun tests/muster-test.mjs. NOTE: also fix muster_module's RUNPATH to include secp256k1 (build-side; -rpath for nim.link libs) so no $ORIGIN hack is needed. Two secondary build fixes proven along the way (secp256k1 RUNPATH, dev-vs-portable variant key). basecamp/flake.nix has the bake-in edits (muster inputs + installedDev) — keep for the fix or revert.

DEEP RESULT — drove P4 acceptance through basecamp+qt-mcp to the last ABI layer, fixed 3 real issues, found the final one. WORKING CHAIN in basecamp: muster-ui builds -> baked into installedDev (dev bundler, keyed linux-amd64-dev = recognized) -> 'M' icon in sidebar -> logos-qt-mcp (basecamp tests harness) app.click('muster_ui') -> muster_module LOADS -> ui-host spawns + 'loaded plugin muster_ui'. Three fixes proven: (F1) muster_module_plugin.so has libsecp256k1.so.5 NEEDED but RUNPATH omits secp's dir (build links -lsecp256k1 without -rpath) -> drop libsecp256k1.so.5 into the module dir ($ORIGIN is in RUNPATH). (F2) dev vs portable variant key: dev core only recognizes linux-amd64-dev; use installDev not installPortable. (F3) logos-view-module-runtime SKEW (basecamp 1fde7d43 vs module-builder 3c3735c2) -> ui-host std::bad_alloc instantiating the view; pinning module-builder's logos-view-module-runtime to 1fde7d43bb2d FIXES the crash. REMAINING (the wall): with view-runtime aligned, ui-host loads muster_ui but 'Timeout waiting for ui-host' — the view never signals ready. Likely the logos-cpp-sdk SKEW (basecamp 4b66dac0 vs module-builder e3744fb8) blocking the capability-token/LogosAPI handshake ('Failed to register token with capability module for: muster_module' -> checkHealth()'s modules().muster_module.health() can't complete). BUT aligning cpp-sdk to 4b66dac0 REGRESSES to bad_alloc — the nim-cdylib-authoring codegen is written against cpp-sdk e3744fb8 and its generated view-glue breaks on 4b66dac0. So the true root fix is STACK ALIGNMENT: update the module-builder's Nim-cdylib codegen to basecamp's logos-cpp-sdk 4b66dac0 (+ keep view-runtime 1fde7d43), so muster-ui's plugin is fully ABI-compatible with basecamp's ui-host. That is upstream codegen work (the plan's 'revalidate the stack table each phase'). Edits left: basecamp/flake.nix (muster bake-in, installDev), module-builder/flake.nix (view-runtime pinned to 1fde7d43; cpp-sdk reverted to unpinned). muster-side is DONE + committed; the block is the module-builder<->basecamp SDK rev alignment.

payload.description:
Decouple muster-ui's build from muster_module's Nim-cdylib builder so the QML view-glue compiles against basecamp's coherent logos-cpp-sdk 4b66dac0 / logos-view-module-runtime 1fde7d43 and instantiates without std::bad_alloc — the render blocker in exo-c6a. muster-ui is already C++/QtRO (same architecture as demo/muster-ui); the only change is which module-builder it follows. Spec: docs/02-implementation-plan.md ADR-013.

Change set: (1) ui/flake.nix — replace logos-module-builder.follows=muster_module/logos-module-builder with a coherent pin (basecamp's builder rev, or follow chat_module/logos-module-builder like the demo); keep muster_module input only for its muster.lidl (typed-client codegen) + runtime presence, built by its own flake. (2) ui/metadata.json — add coherent-host runtime nix.packages (demo carries qt6.qtdeclarative, zstd, krb5, abseil-cpp). (3) ui/src/* — no rewrite; backend keeps modules().muster_module.health()/describe()/propose().

Spike to confirm before committing: (a) a non-cdylib builder can codegen the muster_module typed client from its LIDL when the module was built by a different (cdylib) builder — demo's lez_core says yes but muster_module is Nim-behind-cdylib, verify the flake exposes what codegen reads; (b) string returns marshal over the bus on the coherent chain (health->ok, describe->JSON, propose->id) — the exo-526 concern; (c) libsecp256k1 RUNPATH fix still applies ($ORIGIN drop or -rpath).

Accept: muster-ui renders in basecamp under xvfb-run + QT_QUICK_BACKEND=software; health probe shows muster_module.health()->ok; propose drives the re-materialization strip (effect -> real re-derived safeTxHash) via the logos-qt-mcp flow. Reversible: reconverge to the single-builder chain when exo-c6a's upstream cpp-sdk bump ships.
payload.title: ADR-013: build muster-ui on a basecamp-coherent builder (exo-c6a workaround)

payload.body: ADR-013 (exo-193) filed as the non-upstream unblock path: build muster-ui on a basecamp-coherent builder instead of muster_module's Nim-cdylib builder, keeping this issue for the upstream logos-cpp-sdk 4b66dac0 codegen bump. The two are parallel — either one unblocks the P4 render; ADR-013 does not wait on upstream. Spec in docs/02-implementation-plan.md ADR-013.

SPIKE finding 1 — exo-c6a's rev table has ROTTED (platform moved since 2026-08-20). Cross-checked flake.locks today:
- basecamp's recorded exo-c6a values are gone: view-module-runtime '1fde7d43' appears in NEITHER basecamp's nor the local builder's lock anymore. basecamp now pins module-builder rev 4717b9af35d8.
- cpp-sdk '4b66dac0' and view-runtime '3c3735c2' now appear in BOTH basecamp's and the local nim-cdylib builder's dependency graphs; cpp-sdk 'e3744fb8' (exo-c6a's builder value) is in the local builder's graph but NOT basecamp's.
- both locks carry MANY nodes per input (nested graph), so 'the' effective rev can't be read from lock text alone — must eval or inspect built artifacts to get the rev the ui-host actually links.
IMPLICATION: the specific pins in ADR-013 (4b66dac0 / 1fde7d43) are illustrative, already stale, and must be RE-MEASURED against current basecamp. The ADR's *approach* is unaffected and in fact more rot-resistant: 'follow basecamp's builder (currently 4717b9af)' beats 'pin these exact revs'. Also note: ui/flake.lock is gitignored (machine-local path inputs) and currently absent.

SPIKE finding 2 — MECHANISM VALIDATED (source trace of logos-module-builder). The core ADR-013 assumption holds:
- The typed modules().muster_module.* client is generated + compiled by the CONSUMING UI module's builder (A), NOT the module's builder (B). buildCppPlugin.nix:221-226; intent at mkLogosModule.nix:170-174.
- It reads only muster_module's published .lidl output (packages.<sys>.lidl); for a cdylib module that's a straight copy of committed muster.lidl (mkLogosModule.nix:791-795). The module is PARSED, never rebuilt (Q4). Precondition: muster_module must expose the 'lidl' output — it does (interface cdylib + codegen.lidl). If it ever stops, consumer falls into a transitional header path that DOES rebuild the dep + re-couples (common.nix:141-213).
- Client + view-glue compile against the UI builder A's OWN cpp-sdk/qt-sdk/protocol pins (buildCppPlugin.nix:111-131, 207-218). => build muster-ui under basecamp's builder and its view-glue ABI-matches basecamp's ui-host.

CORRECTION to exo-c6a: logos-view-module-runtime is NOT a plugin compile input at all — it's threaded only into logos-standalone-app (runtime host). exo-c6a's 'view-runtime skew' was a red herring for the compile; the compile-relevant roots are cpp-sdk/qt-sdk/protocol. The fix is 'build the UI under basecamp's builder', not 'pin view-runtime'.

VERDICT: spike (a) GREEN on mechanism. Concrete next step: set ui/flake.nix logos-module-builder to basecamp's current builder (4717b9af), nix build .#lgx, install into a basecamp --user-dir, render under xvfb + QT_QUICK_BACKEND=software, assert health()->ok. Remaining risks are runtime-only: bus string-marshalling (exo-526) and libsecp256k1 RUNPATH — only the build+run reveals them.

SPIKE finding 3 — BUILD GREEN (actual build, not just source trace). Set ui/flake.nix logos-module-builder to basecamp's builder 4717b9af (dropping the follows=muster_module coupling); nix build ./ui#lgx exited 0. Log proves the mechanism:
  Running logos-cpp-generator (api-style=qt)...
  Generating deps from LIDL: muster_module
  Generated dependency wrapper: muster_module_api.h (class MusterModule, 6 methods, 0 events)
  logos-module-builder: generating ui plugin glue (muster_ui)...
=> the coherent builder generated the typed muster_module client (all 6 methods) from its .lidl + compiled the view-glue, producing logos-muster_ui-module.lgx (716KB, variant linux-amd64-dev). muster_module was READ (logos-muster_module-lidl.drv, a copy), NOT rebuilt — confirming Q4. Generators pulled from cache.nix.logos.co (substituter works for this box). This is the exact build exo-c6a blocked under the cdylib builder.

CAVEAT: build-green != render-works. exo-c6a's std::bad_alloc was at RUNTIME view instantiation in basecamp's ui-host, not at build. The build proves compile-ABI-compat; the decisive test is still the RENDER — install the .lgx into a basecamp --user-dir (dev variant), load under xvfb + QT_QUICK_BACKEND=software, drive via logos-qt-mcp, assert health()->ok + the re-materialization strip. Remaining runtime risks unchanged: bus marshalling (exo-526), libsecp256k1 RUNPATH. ui/flake.nix edit held local (not committed) pending render verification.

SPIKE finding 4 — RENDER: ADR-013 core PROVEN, secp blocker fixed. Baked muster into logos-basecamp installedDev (via muster's own pre-built .install outputs — basecamp's installDev re-bundle of .lib fails with 'qml/Main.qml not found', a bundler-version skew; the standalone install is self-consistent). Ran basecamp offscreen + logos-qt-mcp driver. RESULT:
  ui-host: loaded plugin "muster_ui" from ".../muster_ui_plugin.so"  <-- NO std::bad_alloc
=> the coherent-built muster_ui view-glue INSTANTIATES in basecamp's ui-host. This is exactly the exo-c6a crash, GONE. ADR-013's core claim is proven at runtime.

The render still failed end-to-end, but for an ORTHOGONAL reason = exo-c6a's F1 (secp256k1), not ADR-013: muster_module failed to load ('libsecp256k1.so.5: cannot open shared object file'). logos_host UNSETS LD_LIBRARY_PATH for module subprocesses (confirmed: unsetenv(LD_LIBRARY_PATH) in the binary), so env injection can't fix it — only the plugin's own RUNPATH. Dead module -> health() times out (20s) -> ui-host never signals ready -> view not shown.

FIXED F1 properly (the 'real fix' exo-c6a named) in the module-builder: nim.link libs (metadata codegen.nim.link, e.g. secp256k1) now get their nix lib dirs appended to the plugin's INSTALL_RPATH. Edits: lib/mkLogosModule.nix passes -DLOGOS_MODULE_NIM_LINK_RPATHS=<runtimePkgs lib dirs>; cmake/LogosModule.cmake appends them to INSTALL_RPATH ('$ORIGIN:<dir>'). Verified: ldd now resolves libsecp256k1.so.5 via RUNPATH, no LD_LIBRARY_PATH. This is a general builder fix (any Nim module with external FFI libs), a clean contribution back like PR #202. Rebuilding basecamp to re-run the full render.

SPIKE COMPLETE — ADR-013 PROVEN END-TO-END. logos-qt-mcp driver in basecamp (offscreen): 2 passed, 0 failed.
  ✓ muster_ui: the view instantiates and renders (header + composer visible) — the exo-c6a bad_alloc is GONE
  ✓ muster_ui: muster_module.health() marshals to ok — exo-526 clean on the coherent chain
The coherent-built UI renders in basecamp's ui-host AND the real muster_module engine loads + responds. This is the running, visible, real-engine Muster UI that exo-c6a blocked, achieved WITHOUT the upstream codegen fix.

Three changes made this work (across three repos):
1. muster/ui/flake.nix (COMMITTABLE, the ADR-013 fix): logos-module-builder.url pinned to basecamp's builder 4717b9af, dropping follows=muster_module. muster_module stays an input only for its .lidl (typed client codegen), built by its own cdylib builder. => client + view-glue compile against basecamp-coherent cpp-sdk/qt-sdk, ABI-match the ui-host.
2. logos-module-builder (UPSTREAM, needs PR — like #202): the secp/nim.link RUNPATH fix. mkLogosModule.nix passes -DLOGOS_MODULE_NIM_LINK_RPATHS=<runtime lib dirs>; LogosModule.cmake appends to INSTALL_RPATH. Fixes non-bundled hosts (logoscore). NOT enough for basecamp — see #3.
3. logos-basecamp (TEST-ONLY): co-locate libsecp256k1.so.5 in modules/muster_module/ (). basecamp's app.nix strips external module RUNPATH entries (removeReferencesTo, keeps only $ORIGIN) + logos-core unsets LD_LIBRARY_PATH, so the rpath fix alone is stripped away; only a co-located .so survives. The real upstream fix belongs in the builder (stage nim.link .so files INTO the module dir, not just rpath) OR basecamp should stop stripping module rpaths — both are follow-ups.

NEXT: commit muster/ui/flake.nix; file the module-builder rpath+co-location fix upstream; note the basecamp rpath-stripping as a separate upstream issue. exo-c6a can stay open for the upstream codegen path, but ADR-013 is a working unblock TODAY.

P4 acceptance harness LANDED at ui/tests/muster-ui-test.mjs (+ README). Drives muster-ui in basecamp via logos-qt-mcp, offscreen: 3/3 green — render, health()->ok, and propose->real re-materialization strip (module re-derives the EIP-712 safeTxHash from the effect; describe() shows the real 2-of-3 Safe on chain 31337). Screenshot artifact captured (muster-ui.png). README documents the app-under-test provisioning (local basecamp bake-in + secp co-location) until the two supporting fixes land upstream.

Honest model: client never holds keys — owner pastes a 65-byte signature over the safeTxHash; backend calls muster_module.approve(intentId, sigHex), which verifies it recovers to an owner. Uses today's module surface (approve/status). Changes: ui/src/muster_ui.rep (SLOT approve + collected/threshold PROPs), muster_ui_backend.{h,cpp} (approve override -> modules().muster_module.approve), ui/qml/Main.qml (paste-sig field + Add-signature button in the intent card, show collected/threshold). Extend ui/tests/muster-ui-test.mjs to drive approve to executable with pre-signed anvil owner sigs.
payload.title: UI: wire approve + lifecycle (collecting → executable)

payload.body: DONE. approve + lifecycle wired end-to-end and verified in basecamp (4/4 harness green). Changes: ui/src/muster_ui.rep (SLOT approve), muster_ui_backend.{h,cpp} (approve -> modules().muster_module.approve; honest 'signature not counted' when a sig doesn't recover to an owner), ui/qml/Main.qml (collectable prop, paste-signature field + Add-signature button, threshold-met notice with objectName executableNotice). Screenshot shows the status rail lit proposed/collecting/ready. UI: submit SLOT + Submit-on-chain button + submitting/final states. Verified end-to-end in basecamp (5/5 harness): recipient received 1000 wei, Safe nonce 1, finality read from chain. Module: muster_module.nim musterSubmit (gEffects/gSigs stored on propose/approve), regenerated muster_gen.nim (7 methods). Needs anvil + MiniSafe deployed for the submit test.
payload.title: UI: submit executable intent on-chain → final

payload.description: Polish the single-instance walkthrough before P3: (1) surface lastError prominently and in-context across propose/approve/submit (bad sig 'not counted', RPC unreachable, propose failure), with a dedicated error row; (2) a reset/new-proposal affordance so the walkthrough can be re-run cleanly (backend clears intent PROPs). Add harness tests: a non-owner signature is rejected with a visible error and state stays collecting; reset returns to a fresh composer.
payload.title: UI polish: honest error surfacing + reset for the walkthrough

payload.body: DONE (6/6 harness green). Honest error surfacing + reset landed. Key correctness fix: musterApprove now EXPLICITLY refuses a signature that doesn't recover to a configured owner (returns 'rejected', never advances the intent) — the previous UI heuristic (newState==prev) missed it because ieContribute transitions proposed->collecting unconditionally (invariant 6: core doesn't read bytes; driver decides counting). Also dedups already-counted owner sigs as 'rejected'. UI: page-level error banner (objectName errorBanner/errorText) showing the module's own reason; reset (backend clears intent PROPs) via 'New proposal' (error banner, any-error recovery) and 'Start a new proposal' (final). Tests: non-owner sig rejected + error shown + intent held; reset clears intentCard.

payload.description: Consume logos-delivery-module behind the Transport interface (ADR-006, resolved); resolve ADR-010 (build-vs-consume logos-chat-module) at phase start. Accept: the P2 flow runs between clients on separate networks through store nodes; a member added mid-conversation provably cannot decrypt earlier epochs (F-16); kill a client mid-collection, restart, contribution still lands (R-1/R-2/R-4).
payload.title: P3: real transport + encryption

payload.description: Re-validate the stack table against upstream HEADs, then decide build-vs-consume logos-chat-module. Deciding questions: (1) curve conflict — is chat-module identity Ed25519 while Muster signs secp256k1, at current HEAD? (2) does its membership model re-key forward PROVABLY (F-16), and can we VERIFY not just trust it? (3) does it leak signer identity (FS-7)? (4) persistent identity — logos_chat::open() mints an unpersisted account; is there an IdentityStore the facade skips? Also confirm logos-delivery-module's API (content topics, pub/sub with delivery events, store queries) still matches ADR-006. Note: local clone is logos-chatsdk-module; demo pins github:logos-co/logos-chat-module/v0.2.2 — reconcile the naming.
payload.title: ADR-010: resolve chat-module build-vs-consume (P3 decision gate)

payload.body: RESOLVED: BUILD Muster's epoch layer for F-16; consume only logos-delivery-module (ADR-006). Code-level investigation of logos-chat-module v0.2.2 + libchat (logos-messaging, pinned 5c55c2ee 2026-07-26). Naming: local logos-chatsdk-module is a stale unrelated C++ thing, NOT a rename; real crypto core is logos-messaging/libchat. Findings: (Q1 curve) identity is Ed25519/X25519, secp256k1 only transitive via alloy — no binding to Muster's secp256k1 Safe key; F-9 intersection would need a binding libchat doesn't provide. (Q2 F-16) groups are DeMLS/openmls; joiner forward-secrecy is INHERITED+TRUSTED from MLS with NO libchat test proving the negative; member REMOVAL not implemented at all (no remove_member in core/conversations or chat_module.lidl) — removal half of F-16 absent. (Q3 FS-7) MLS leaf credential binds a stable identity+Ed25519 key to every message/commit; message_received surfaces directory-verified sender — no unlinkable mode; anonymous driver deanonymized. (Q4 persistence) PERSISTENCE_ENABLED=false, openmls on MemoryStorage — ephemeral, can't survive R-4/R-6 restart; IdentityStore exists in core/sqlite but facade doesn't use it. (Q5 delivery) confirms ADR-006: content topics, publish, subscribe, storeQuery, reliable channels; embeds its own Waku node. Decision recorded in plan ADR-010.

payload.description: Define the Transport interface (F-15: content topics, publish with delivery/propagation events, subscribe, store queries, channels) in module/src/transport/, plus a local/in-memory implementation for integration tests (working agreement: tests use local transport, never mock it). The delivery_module-backed impl (consume logos-delivery-module via the logos API) follows once the interface + local impl are proven. Codes against the interface; delivery binds at runtime (ADR-006). Part of P3 epic exo-6dc.
payload.title: P3: Transport interface + local/in-memory impl

payload.body: DONE: Transport interface + in-memory LocalTransport committed (7dea6a8), 5/5 tests (live exchange, deterministic content address, offline catchup via store, idempotent ingest R-2/R-4, topic isolation). module/src/transport/transport.nim + tests/transport_test.nim.

payload.description: Wire the delivery-backed Transport by consuming logos-delivery-module over the logos API. BLOCKER/scope: there is no Nim caller-side SDK — inter-module calls go through the lp_* C ABI from logos-protocol, which the logos-rust-sdk binds (~2145 lines: binds lp_*, serializes params, drives callback trampolines, delivers results over channels; Client::bind(name)->LogosModuleSDK.plugin(name)). Need a Nim binding of the lp_* subset for delivery's 4 methods (createNode/start/subscribe/send) + the messageReceived/connectionStateChanged events, then a DeliveryTransport: Transport impl over it. muster_module declares delivery_module as a dependency (metadata.json). This is the caller-side analog of muster_gen's callee-side codegen. Depends on exo-c8b (interface, done). Part of P3 epic exo-6dc.
payload.title: P3: delivery-backed Transport (Nim lp_* outbound-call binding + delivery client)

payload.body: Delivery-backed Transport BUILT (binding validated end-to-end). module/src/transport/lp_ffi.nim mirrors the rust-sdk src/ffi.rs (~12 lp_* extern decls: lp_client_create/lp_invoke/lp_invoke_async/lp_subscribe/lp_string_free/… + the {"_bytes":"<base64url,unpadded>"} bstr codec from bytes.rs). module/src/transport/delivery.nim = DeliveryTransport : Transport over it (publish=lp_invoke send, subscribe=lp_invoke subscribe + lp_subscribe messageReceived event routing, storeQuery best-effort). VERIFIED: (1) both type-check; (2) the lp_* symbols are exported (T) in liblogos_protocol.a which muster_module already links; (3) the module PLUGIN builds+links with lp_protocol_version() called from describe() — the FFI resolves in the real plugin. So my earlier '2145-line Nim SDK' framing was wrong: it's a small FFI over the same C ABI both SDKs bind, no Rust needed. REMAINING (next increment): wire Transport into the coordination flow (multi-instance), a live two-instance test over a real delivery node, harden the messageReceived callback's foreign-thread GC seam (storage-nim abandoned-flag pattern), and switch send to lp_invoke_async (sync send blocks the dispatch thread on delivery's accept handshake, per the chat module).

payload.description: Build the per-conversation epoch layer (ADR-002 default): a symmetric epoch key encrypts envelopes (AEAD, libsodium); the epoch key is ECIES-wrapped to each member's secp256k1 pubkey (reusing the Safe key, recovered from their signatures — no second curve). Re-key on every membership change: add -> new epoch, joiner gets only the new key (can't decrypt earlier epochs, F-16 forward secrecy); remove -> rotate, removed member can't read new epochs. F-16 acceptance test: a member added mid-conversation provably cannot decrypt earlier epochs (verify, not trust — the ADR-010 bar). Builds against LocalTransport. DONE so far: ECDH primitive (secp256k1 tweak_mul, since nixpkgs secp lacks the ecdh module) + pubkey recovery, 3/3 tested. REMAINING: AEAD (libsodium bind), epoch/membership/re-key structure, F-16 property test. Part of P3 epic exo-6dc.
payload.title: P3: F-16 epoch encryption (ECIES-secp256k1 wrap, re-key on membership change)

payload.body: ConversationCrypto seam defined (module/src/crypto/conversation.nim) — the swappable boundary per the amended ADR-010: seal/open/addMember/removeMember/members/epoch. Our EpochCrypto (ECIES-secp256k1) will be a labeled stopgap behind it; native logos-chat-module binds here once it ships persistence+removal. Members identified by secp256k1 PubKey (no second curve). Type-checks. REMAINING for the stopgap impl: AEAD (libsodium secretbox bind), ECIES wrap/unwrap (ecdh+AEAD, ecdh primitive already done), the epoch/membership/re-key structure, and the F-16 property test (joiner can't open earlier epochs).

EpochCrypto STOPGAP DONE — F-16 verified in code (5/5). module/src/crypto/sodium.nim (libsodium secretbox AEAD bind, symbols confirmed) + epoch_crypto.nim (ECIES-secp256k1: ephemeral key -> ecdh -> secretbox wraps a per-epoch key to each member's secp256k1 pubkey; per-conversation epochs; re-key on add/remove) behind the ConversationCrypto interface. tests/epoch_crypto_test.nim asserts the F-16 property (the ADR-010 'verify not trust' bar): a member added at epoch 2 CANNOT open an epoch-1 envelope; a removed member CANNOT open a later epoch; a non-recipient can't unwrap a grant. Members = secp256k1 pubkeys (no second curve). Explicitly a stopgap: native chat binds the same interface once it ships persistence+removal. REMAINING (next increment, not this session): wire ConversationCrypto+Transport into the multi-instance coordination flow (publish sealed intent events, ingest+open peer events), add libsodium to the module nix.packages when wired, live two-instance test.

payload.description: Operation-based Keystore interface (sign/ecdh/address/pubKey) so a Keycard/OS-keystore backend can slot behind it later. First impl: FileKeystore persisting an Argon2id-encrypted secp256k1 keyfile. Unblocks the P3 hosted coordination surface (one persistent secp256k1 key reused for Safe signing + epoch ECDH, ADR-010).

payload.description: Built module/tools/headless-host/ — a coherent in-process logos-core host that loads muster+delivery with the capability gate off and invokes their methods headless (health/identity/describe + the single-instance coordinate fold join->propose->intents with a re-derived safeTxHash). LANDED. The two-instance LIVE wire (two hosts converging over a real Waku network) is blocked by two infra gaps, diagnosed in docs/labbook/two-instance-live-wire-blockers.md: (1) muster's lp->delivery bridge does not boot the Waku node in this bespoke host (coordinate_join emits zero Waku logs vs 66 from a direct QRO createNode; single-instance folds work only because publish() writes the local log first); (2) the bundled logos.test preset ships no bootstrap nodes (seed node, no discovery), and reading a peer's multiaddr via getNodeInfo over QRO hangs behind delivery's thread-blocking start(). Unblock needs a reachable delivery bootstrap node (+ENR in entryNodes) and/or host-side lp-bridge wiring.
payload.title: Two-instance live wire: coherent headless host + two infra blockers

payload.body: Blocker 2 (discovery) SOLVED by piggybacking off the Logos delivery fleet (user suggestion). https://fleets.logos.co/data.json lists logos-node-delivery: logos.test=cluster 2 (6 nodes), logos.dev=cluster 3. payload.body: Landed 2026-09-01 (commit 28d7f64). Cross-host store catchup tightened from an ~8s whole-topic re-fetch to a ~1s time-windowed poll. Changes: (a) delivery.nim time-windows each steady-state query (timeStart = now - MUSTER_CATCHUP_LOOKBACK_MS, default 60s; first DeepCatchupTicks=3 per topic still deep-fetch full history so late joiners catch up); (b) period 8s->1s via MUSTER_CATCHUP_MS (floor 200ms); (c) Room.qml live-refresh 3s->1s and the offscreen self-test timer 6s->1s (both drive poll()); (d) join-request retry 5s->3s. Measured offscreen on the live logos.test fleet: joiner announce -> founder sees request ~1.0s; announce -> both members=2 ~3.0s (was ~8s+). Two instances still converge (members=2 both). Remaining (optional further polish, not blocking): rotate the store peer across entryNodes for resilience; fix delivery's live-relay receive so messages arrive push-not-poll (delivery-internal). (2) The proper latency fix below the poll floor: muster's delivery node runs mode=Core (relay), so on our sparse shard nothing is pushed and receive rides store polling. mode=Edge makes it a light node receiving via Filter (service node pushes matching messages) — no relay mesh needed. Try Edge; if the fleet nodes push our topic, wire it and keep store catchup as fallback (push-primary, poll-backup).

payload.body: Done 2026-09-02. (1) Store-peer ROTATION landed: fireCatchup round-robins the storeQuery across all entryNodes (was entryNodes[0] only), so a down/throttling store node costs one ~1s tick not the whole catchup. Verified offscreen — one instance cycled evenly across all 6 fleet nodes while still converging (members=2 both). (2) Real-time PUSH receive INVESTIGATED and found blocked upstream — NOT fixable from muster. Findings: a light node (mode:Edge) mounts the Waku filter+lightpush clients and its filter client DOES receive message pushes on our sparse shard /waku/2/rs/2/5 on BOTH peers (14-16/run). But the closed liblogosdelivery v0.38.1 kernel only converts some pushes into message_received events (founder 8, joiner 0 in a 2-node run); the delivery C++ faithfully forwards whatever the kernel emits. Core vs Edge is IDENTICAL (8/0 in both) — the drop is the kernel's recv->event path, tracking subscribe-order/role, not relay-vs-filter. So muster has no lever and store-poll (~1s, exo-38e) stays the reliable receive path until an upstream kernel fix surfaces receipts as message_received for every subscriber. Full evidence + corrected labbook theory in docs/labbook/two-instance-live-wire-blockers.md.

payload.description:
Verified 2026-09-02 against exophial 0.2.0+dc69cd1d by calling spec_oracle.run_spec(Spec.from_dict(...), Path('.')) — the same in-process entrypoint the reducer's completion gate uses — over all 12 contracts/specs/derived-exo-*.spec.json at HEAD.

RESULT: 43 checks, 0 pass. 42 fail with the identical error:
  artifact stdout is not valid JSON: Extra data: line 2 column 1 (char N)

ROOT CAUSE (not environmental — supersedes the stale exo-a5d hypothesis, which was closed as resolved 2026-08-20 and whose fix still works). nim resolves (/usr/local/bin/nim, Nim 2.2.10), every probe compiles and exits 0. exophial's spec_oracle._parse_measurement does json.loads(stdout) on the WHOLE buffer, so an artifact must emit EXACTLY ONE JSON document. Our 43 probes emit JSONL — one observation per line:
  $ nim r -d:release tests/probes/probe_materialization_derivation_agrees.nim
  {"agrees": true}
  {"agrees": true}
  ...

Two contracts are violated:
1. property_test TRACE form (_check_trace_invariant): the oracle wants a single {"traces": [[state, ...], ...]} object, which it forwards to trace_monitor.py for rtamt temporal evaluation. Our probes emit a bare stream of per-trial objects. The stream IS one trace; it just lacks the envelope.
2. model_check STEPPER form (_run_stepper / _check_model_check): the oracle invokes the stepper with a state as the final argv and expects THAT STATE'S SUCCESSORS. Our steppers ignore the argv entirely and dump the whole reachable space as JSONL. Confirmed: probe_config_reachability_stepper.nim prints identical output with and without a state argument.

The probes are substantively correct — they measure the real invariant and pass by hand. Only the wire format is wrong.

FIX: re-emit all 43 probes under module/tests/probes/ to the oracle's contracts — wrap trace output in {"traces": [[...]]}, and make model_check steppers read the state argv and print only that state's successors. Keep the invariant logic untouched; this is a printing/entry change.

ACCEPTANCE: spec_oracle.run_spec over each of the 12 specs returns ok=True at HEAD. This is the single change that makes exophial's grading loop real in muster for the first time.

Evidence + full analysis: docs/exophial-usage-gaps.md finding G3.

payload.body:
SUPERSEDED AS A HYPOTHESIS (2026-09-02), though this pebble's own fix is intact and still working.

Re-graded all 12 specs at HEAD against exophial 0.2.0+dc69cd1d via spec_oracle.run_spec — the same in-process entrypoint the reducer's completion gate uses. Result: 43 checks, 0 pass.

This pebble's fix HELD: nim is at /usr/local/bin/nim (Nim 2.2.10), every probe compiles, every probe exits 0. Nothing fails for want of nim or secp256k1.

But 42 of 43 checks fail for a reason never diagnosed here: 'artifact stdout is not valid JSON: Extra data: line 2 column 1'. spec_oracle._parse_measurement does json.loads() on the whole stdout buffer, so an artifact must emit exactly ONE JSON document; our probes emit JSONL, one observation per line. Two contracts are violated — the property_test trace form wants {"traces": [[state,...],...]} in one object, and the model_check stepper form wants the successors of the state passed as final argv (our steppers ignore the argv and dump the whole space). Filed as exo-dbc.

The remaining 1 of 43 (probe_return_marshalling_host.nim) fails on a missing nimble 'results' package — identically under a plain shell, so also not this pebble's hermetic-scrub issue. Filed as exo-a7b.

Recording this because docs/exophial-usage-gaps.md (2026-09-01) cited this pebble's hermetic-env theory as the standing explanation for the failed regates. That inference was reasonable but wrong: the environment was fixed here on 2026-08-20 and the regate kept failing for an unrelated, purely mechanical reason. Full evidence in docs/exophial-usage-gaps.md finding G3.

ROOT CAUSE FOUND (2026-09-02) — this is upstream in exophial, not author discipline.

exophial.session_provenance.add_session_trailer (session_provenance.py:109) does:
    return f"{body}\n\n{trailer}\n" if body else f"{trailer}\n"

That blank line before Session-Id is unconditional. Git recognizes only the FINAL contiguous trailer block, so the hook severs every trailer the author wrote from the trailer section — while preserving its own.

Demonstrated live: commit a4b3448 was authored with Tested-Behavior / TDD-Exempt / Co-Authored-By as ONE contiguous block. The commit-msg hook appended Session-Id after a blank line. git log --format='%(trailers:key=Tested-Behavior)' still returns empty.

Across the 271-commit history:
  Session-Id      (hook-written)   parsable on 150 commits
  Tested-Behavior (author-written) parsable on 0 — but present in raw text on 62
  Co-Authored-By  (author-written) parsable on 17 (the commits the hook did not stamp)

So the audit's proposed fix ('write all trailers as one contiguous block') does NOT work — we already do, and it still fails. The real fix is upstream: add_session_trailer should append into the existing trailer block when the message already ends in one, and only insert a blank line when it does not. Added to the upstream asks in exo-aa7.

Muster-side there is nothing to fix beyond waiting for or contributing that change. Retitling accordingly is reasonable.

Context: docs/exophial-usage-gaps.md finding G6.

FOURTH UPSTREAM ASK (2026-09-02): add_session_trailer breaks every other trailer.

exophial.session_provenance.add_session_trailer (session_provenance.py:109):
    return f"{body}\n\n{trailer}\n" if body else f"{trailer}\n"

The blank line is unconditional, so when a commit message already ends in a contiguous trailer block, the hook's Session-Id starts a NEW block and git's parser (git interpret-trailers, %(trailers)) sees only Session-Id. Every author-written Tested-Behavior / TDD-Exempt / Co-Authored-By is orphaned.

Measured on muster's 271-commit history: Session-Id parsable on 150 commits; Tested-Behavior parsable on 0 despite appearing in the raw text of 62; Co-Authored-By parsable on only the 17 commits the hook did not stamp.

ASK: when the message already ends in a trailer block, append into it; insert the blank line only when it does not. This also matters for exophial's own tooling — the module docstring says the point is 'one trailer format, one parser, no drift between writer and INTEGRATE', but the writer currently produces something the standard parser cannot read.

See exo-4ed and docs/exophial-usage-gaps.md finding G6.

From docs/03-session-handoff-2026-09-02.md section 3. Lever: module/src/dcbor/ is already the reference CDE implementation (invariant 5) paired with domain-separated hash-input records.

Rule: an activity renders ONLY from a declared, versioned schema. When no matching schema resolves, show a NAMED failure state — 'schema unknown' plus module name and version. No blank panes, no empty lists: a silent empty view hides the exact problem the upstream argument depends on.

Then write the upstream proposal — promote the CDE encoder and the hash-input record discipline to logos-core, with the rendering failure as the motivating case. Name the second consumer while writing: driver manifests (section 2) need the same schema language.

CHECK AGAINST CLAUDE.md: module/src/schemas/ does NOT exist — there is no CDDL parser and no cdCDDLe in v0 (ADR-009). v0 uses hand-assigned schema ids (muster.event.*.v1) in the profile + schema-id fields. So 'declared, versioned schema' at this stage means the v0 id vocabulary, not a parsed CDDL root. Scope accordingly, or the task silently grows a CDDL parser.

Honesty rule (docs/00-vision.md): the failure state explains what the code already guarantees. DONE WHEN: a stale or missing schema produces a named, screenshot-able failure, and the proposal exists in docs/ with that screenshot in it.

payload.description:
From docs/03-session-handoff-2026-09-02.md section 2. Model: a VS Code extension manifest the host reads WITHOUT loading the extension's code; contributes.configuration is a JSON Schema and the host builds the settings UI from it.

Existing half (per CLAUDE.md + the driver-standard memory): module/src/drivers/ already has the registry, the generic Driver interface (invariant 6: describe/canonicalize/verifyContribution), the conformance suite, and a threshold k-of-n driver proving the seam is generic. What a registry entry does NOT carry is the driver's CONFIGURATION.

Tasks: extend the registry entry with a declared config schema + capability list, kept separate from the call interface (muster.lidl is the seam for calls; this is the seam for settings); version the schema so the host can refuse an entry whose version it does not understand, BY NAME; let the host enumerate and configure a driver before loading it; generate the settings surface from the schema — no per-driver QML; extend the conformance suite so a driver whose declared schema does not match what it actually accepts FAILS; decide config scope now (per-install / per-machine / per-identity / per-room) and put it in the schema.

DEPENDS ON section 3 for the schema language. Invariant 3 guard: plugins never sign, never hold keys, never touch the network — a manifest must not become a capability grant that widens that.

DONE WHEN: safe driver and threshold driver both configure through the generated surface, and conformance fails a driver with a lying manifest.
payload.title: §2 Driver manifests: self-describing drivers with a declared config schema, generated settings surface, conformance check

payload.description:
From docs/03-session-handoff-2026-09-02.md section 4. The status quo is a null cipher: build the system with the null in place, then replace the nulls one at a time. Correspondence principle — the weaker theory is the limiting case of the stronger one, not a different theory.

Already in the code, unnamed: the ChainAdapter seam (EVM adapter = transparent null, mock shielded adapter = the real one at the same seam) and the Transport seam (LocalTransport null, delivery_module real).

THREE AXES, THREE NULLS — keep separate, they do not substitute:
  authentication  (who is speaking now)          null: anonymous     real: bound secp256k1 identity
  provenance      (where from, what path)        null: unattested    real: signed hash-linked log, attested build
  confidentiality (who can read it)              null: plaintext     real: ECIES epochs, shielded adapter
A signed artifact is not a private one; an encrypted channel to an unknown peer is not an authenticated one.

Tasks: name the pattern in docs/ pointing at both existing instances; make the level a TYPED ATTRIBUTE on the seam, not a branch in the code path, with the null carrying the same metadata envelope as the real thing; build the provenance ladder (does not exist yet).

HAZARD to design against: TLS shipped NULL and export-grade suites and got downgrade attacks (FREAK, Logjam). Negotiation itself must be authenticated. The null must be explicit opt-in, displayed, and NEVER a silent fallback when the real option fails. The honesty rules already demand this at the surface; put it in the type too.

Invariant 10 already requires signing be REFUSED when an input's origin is unaccountable — the provenance rung must extend that, not duplicate it. Invariant 9 guard: anonymous drivers stay anonymous, so the authentication null is a legitimate terminal state, not a rung to climb off.

DONE WHEN: a probe shows a failed upgrade refuses rather than falls back, and the active level on all three axes is visible in the UI.
payload.title: §4 The null ladder: name it, type it on the seam, build the provenance rung, probe that failed upgrade REFUSES

payload.description:
Found 2026-09-02 while making the first spec grade green (exo-dbc).

Once probes emit the correct trace envelope, property_test trace-invariant checks reach exophial's trace_monitor, which requires rtamt. The exophial tool venv HAS rtamt 0.3.5 installed, but importing it on the venv's Python 3.14 raises:
  ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'typing.io'; 'typing' is not a package

Cause is not rtamt itself but its pinned dependency antlr4-python3-runtime==4.7, which does 'from typing.io import TextIO' in Lexer.py and Parser.py. typing.io was deprecated in 3.8 and REMOVED in 3.13, so rtamt 0.3.5 cannot import on any Python >= 3.13. exophial 0.2.0+dc69cd1d ships on Python 3.14, so the trace-invariant oracle level is unusable out of the box on this install.

WORKAROUND IN USE: a Python 3.12 venv with rtamt, pointed at via the escape hatch the error message itself offers:
  export SPEC_ORACLE_RTAMT_PYTHON=<venv>/bin/python
Verified: with it set, derived-exo-8e7 grades PASS (3/3), including a discriminating-mutation check (seeded fault -> FAIL with robustness=-1, emitter still exit 0).

This needs a durable home rather than an ad-hoc scratch venv — either pin the interpreter for the rtamt subprocess in muster's own tooling, or upstream: bump antlr4-python3-runtime (checking rtamt's generated parsers still match the runtime version) so rtamt imports on 3.13+.

Blocks every property_test trace-invariant check (19 of 43) from grading on a default install. Related: exo-dbc, exo-aa7.
payload.title: exophial's vendored rtamt is broken on Python 3.14 (antlr4 4.7 imports typing.io)

payload.description:
From docs/03-session-handoff-2026-09-02.md section 5. Model: the curl project — not a product, a process. Signed commits for provenance; every release tarball signed so a consumer can confirm the files were not altered after production; the git repo as authoritative and auditable source of truth, held there by review requirements, a banned-function list, a function complexity ceiling, and a ban on binary blobs and most base64 (both can hide a payload); a written policy on what the project expects from dependencies; and documented verification steps so a consumer can run the check.

SPLIT IN TWO:
  runtime provenance — module/src/intents/provenance + the signed hash-linked log. EXISTS. Answers: where did this intent come from, what path did it take. (Invariant 10, spec derived-exo-3a1.)
  build provenance — DOES NOT EXIST. Section 1 is the precondition: while the build depends on a contributor's machine there is no chain of custody from source to artifact to claim.

STANDARDS TO EVALUATE: in-toto (the one with an actual language — a layout declaring expected steps and who is authorized to perform each, verified against collected link metadata; closest match); SLSA (build track + source track, four levels — vocabulary and level targets); Sigstore/Rekor (signing + append-only transparency log); SPDX or CycloneDX (component inventory).

Tasks: after section 1, produce a reproducible build from a fresh clone (nix does most of this once the pins are gone); sign releases and document the verification steps; draft an in-toto layout for the Muster release chain and see what it costs; write the dependency policy; note the overlap worth writing up — Logos already has a transparency log and a storage layer, so attestations are a native payload rather than a third-party service.

DONE WHEN: a release ships with a signature and documented verification, and the layout draft exists.
payload.title: §5 Build provenance and the supply chain: reproducible fresh-clone build, signed releases, in-toto layout draft, dependency policy

From docs/03-session-handoff-2026-09-02.md section 6. Earlier versions exist for Logos in logos-legos and the v2 logos-workflow-* modules; both need updating against the current logos-core architecture.

Why JACK is the right reference: a connection is legal only when the port types match, and format and rate are settled AT CONNECT TIME, not discovered at runtime. That is the same check as section 3 — a link is valid only if the source's output schema satisfies the sink's input schema. And the null ladder from section 4 becomes port attributes negotiated at the same moment: cipher, credential, and provenance level all settled when the ports connect.

Tasks: pull logos-legos and the logos-workflow-* modules; list what breaks against the current logos-core module interface; replace ad-hoc wiring with typed port negotiation against the declared schemas; carry the three levels from section 4 as port attributes.

Largest and least urgent of the seven. DONE WHEN: the breakage list exists and a design note connects port typing to the CDDL schema work.
payload.title: §6 Source-to-sink pipeline: typed port negotiation over declared schemas (JACK as reference)

Task: diff the logos-core module interface spec (logos-core-poc2, CDDL/dCBOR) against what logos-basecamp actually implements. Produce TWO lists: (a) behavior in the spec that is not implemented, (b) behavior implemented that the spec does not describe. The second list is the translation loss.

Likewise logos-lips branch draft/logos-core-module-specs is an UNMERGED draft, tracked not targeted; where any of it diverges from what logoscore actually loads, the shipping host wins. This is an INTERIM pin on the PR's own rev, not a permanent fork dependency — repoint at logos-co master once #226 merges. It is a real github ref, so a fresh clone resolves it with no local checkout.

exo-865 is done as a blocker: the last machine-local pin in module/ is gone. Remaining under exo-414 is ui/flake.nix's git+file:///home/petty/... muster_module pin, the README truth pass, and the fresh-clone CI job.

PROGRESS + a finding.

DONE (exo-865): module/flake.nix no longer carries a machine-local pin. It now reads
  github:corpetty/logos-module-builder/720ac2f  (the rev of logos-co/logos-module-builder#226)
Both variants build from it, and a fresh clone of this branch was built with no access to the local builder checkout.

FINDING worth folding into this task and into exo-968 (§5 build provenance): module/flake.lock is GITIGNORED (.gitignore:19). So a fresh clone has no lock at all. The builder input is safe — it is pinned by rev in the url — but every TRANSITIVE input (nixpkgs, logos-nix, the sdks, rust-overlay, logos-delivery-module's own closure) resolves fresh at build time. Two consequences:
  1. §1's 'clone it and build' works today but is not reproducible ACROSS TIME — the same clone built next month can resolve different transitive inputs.
  2. §5 wants a reproducible build from a fresh clone as the precondition for any build-provenance claim. An unpinned transitive closure means there is nothing to attest to. in-toto/SLSA both assume the inputs are pinned.
Committing module/flake.lock (and ui/flake.lock, check whether it is ignored too) is the obvious fix, and is cheap. Worth deciding before writing the CI job, because the CI job is what would otherwise silently paper over it by always building from a warm cache.

STILL OPEN under this pebble:

Not a trivial swap: the existing comment records that a path: input copies untracked build symlinks and breaks muster_module's Nim build, which is why git+file was chosen. Options are (a) github:corpetty/muster?dir=module — works from a fresh clone but pins ui to a PUSHED module commit, so local module iteration needs a push each time; (b) a root flake.nix exposing both module and ui so they reference each other through self, which is the clean fix and the one that actually makes 'clone and make run' true; (c) a source filter that makes path: ignore untracked files. Recommend (b).
  - README.md / module/README.md / module/tests/README.md truth pass — must wait until ui/ is fixed too, or the READMEs would claim a fresh-clone 'make run' that still does not work.

So the module half of the fresh-clone requirement is genuinely met, not merely locally cached. Closing.

The P4 render harness cannot produce a coherent bake with CURRENT muster_ui: muster_module_plugin.so fails to load with 'undefined symbol: logos_module_set_unload_done_callback', so the module process crashes and the whole muster_ui view never instantiates (all 9 harness tests fail; the launcher is found but no content renders).

Root cause (diagnosed 2026-09-03, inherent — reproduced with clean natural nix resolution, not caused by follows experiments): muster's builder pins — logos-co/logos-module-builder@4717b9af (ui) and corpetty/logos-module-builder@720ac2f (module) — resolve logos-cpp-sdk@58c65737, whose module-load contract has the MODULE import logos_module_set_unload_done_callback from the host. basecamp's host is built from logos-cpp-sdk@8554ecd7, where the MODULE DEFINES that symbol (basecamp's own package_manager/package_downloader plugins export it, T). So muster's plugin imports a symbol the host doesn't provide → crash.

Why now: the 6/9-passing bake used muster_ui@55540084 (the minimal lifecycle-spike UI) whose cpp-sdk then matched basecamp; upstream cpp-sdk has since advanced and basecamp advanced its host, reopening the exo-c6a/exo-193 skew. The current full product UI (Room/MusterCard/etc.) never gets to render because the module dies first.

Tried and rejected: follows-pinning muster's builder logos-cpp-sdk (and qt-sdk/view-runtime) to basecamp's fixes the runtime contract but BREAKS the build ('logos-qt-sdk not found' — the two SDK generations are mutually incompatible in layout). No flake-follows bridges build+runtime.

Fix direction: bump muster's builder pins (module/flake.nix, ui/flake.nix) to a logos-module-builder rev whose logos-cpp-sdk generation matches basecamp's current host (8554ecd7-era), then verify muster still builds (may cascade Nim/C++ glue changes) and that the symbol flips to defined. Alternatively pin basecamp's host to muster's SDK generation. Evidence + full trace in docs/labbook/basecamp-sdk-skew-unload-callback.md.

payload.description: Add module/src/drivers/frost.nim: the first driver with describe().rounds=2, so the core's round-advancement path (Collection.submit advancing col.round, driven only by describe()) gets a real driver behind it — currently only the stub exercises rounds>1, and Safe/threshold are all r=1. Models FROST's 2-round structure (commit round → sign round, k-of-n each, named Ed25519 roster) reusing curve25519 signatures as the per-round authenticated contribution; acceptance is round-agnostic (conformance's convergence test reuses one contribution across both rounds). Passes checkConformance via tests/conformance_test.nim; registry 'frost' arm; driverForKind arm for room selection. SCAFFOLD boundary documented: no real Schnorr nonce-commitment aggregation, and the room fold needs a round-aware contribution dedup (reduceIntents dedups one contribution per member per intent → stalls a per-round protocol at round 2) — filed separately.
payload.title: 2-round FROST-style driver — exercise the multi-round core path

payload.description: reduceIntents (module/src/coordination/intents.nim) dedups contributions by <id>/<contributor> — one contribution per member per intent. That is correct for single-round drivers (Safe/threshold) but stalls any rounds>1 driver at round 2: k members reach the round-1 threshold, the core advances to round 2, and then every member is already spent, so round 2 never reaches k and the intent never becomes executable. To run the 2-round FROST driver (exo-ade) END TO END IN A ROOM: (1) make the contribute event carry a round (the key already parses p[3]; add a round segment), (2) dedup by <id>/<round>/<contributor>, and (3) surface the round in coordinate_contribute + the UI approve affordance. The core Collection + lifecycle already advance rounds correctly (frost_test proves it); only the room fold's dedup and the contribute surface need the round. Until then FROST is NOT added to driverForKind / the room picker (it would be selectable but stall).
payload.title: Round-aware contribution dedup so multi-round drivers run in a room

payload.description: Muster's education mission (docs/00-vision): a member entering a room must see HOW the room reached its current state, and see updates as they happen. Fold the coordination log into a human-readable activity timeline — joined/asked/admitted/re-keyed(epoch), proposed, approved (M of N), submitted, settled(final) — interleaved with chat, shown in the room. Additive: a new fold over the existing sealed log (state=reduce(log)), no new signing path.

payload.description: Entering a room currently auto-reads myAddress from settings.identity.address (Room.qml:86) — against Muster's ask-then-selectively-disclose principle. On entry, ASK which secp/payment account to attach (from wallet_accounts); disclose the address only on an explicit action (propose / address-share). NB the ENCRYPTION identity is required to join (epoch key) — this is about the payment/secp address you act and settle as, and what the room learns about you.
payload.title: Ask-then-disclose the room-attached address (not auto-present on entry)

payload.description: The composer sends a bare amount to the Safe with no notion of what (Room.qml:158). Populate it from the attached account's real wallet_balances — pick a real asset and available amount, can't over-send. Depends on the attached-account decision (ask-then-disclose). ETH settles via the Safe driver today; label anything not yet settleable honestly rather than implying it works.
payload.title: Compose from real holdings: pick asset+amount from the attached account's balances

payload.description: Surface liveness of the infrastructure the room relies on: RPC reachable (eth_chainId/blockNumber), delivery node up + peer count.
