payload.description: reduceActivity (exo-aa8) folds coordination-state transitions from the log, but join/admit/re-key are transport CONTROL frames (session.nim: requestJoin/admit publish FrameJoinRequest/FrameControl), not log events, so they don't appear in the Room history feed. Record a membership event on admit (e.g. 'membership/epoch/<n>' naming the admitted member, sealed under the new epoch) and add akAdmit/akRekey entries to reduceActivity, so a member sees 'X was admitted — room re-keyed to epoch N (F-16)' in history. Keep it consistent with F-16 (the entry is sealed to the epoch it describes) and FS-7 (anonymous drivers name nothing). Relates to exo-080 (ask-then-disclose).
payload.title: Record membership transitions as log events so admits show in Room history

payload.description: Every Logos module that lets a user 'do something' becomes a Muster driver, so the module is infrastructure for doing that thing with others. payload.description: Design: docs/design/action-manifest.md. Five wants (2026-09-15): data-provenance proofs for all group actions; muster as the emergent security/permissions protocol for Logos (what am I allowing before it is allowed); visualizing information flow + disclosure within a group; all of it deterministic from what a module's contract exposes; and a proposal card that tells every participant what the action will do, what it needs, what it touches, what will happen, how agreement is made, and lets them install missing dependencies, authorize, approve, or deny. Ground: the PriFi imperative-vs-motivational credibility axis — muster classifies commitments (per link, per observer), never scores them. Relates to exo-1ec.4 (driver CONFIG manifest — settings seam; this epic is the per-ACTION manifest), exo-1ec.5 (provenance rung), exo-275 (membership events in the log).

Conformance gains: manifest stable, declared+consistent, agreement == describe(). All six drivers (stub, safe, threshold, frost, invoke, eip191) declare. lez_core.toDisclosureRows(disclosureOf(rail)) so the LEZ square is the first real per-action disclosure. Tests: manifest_test (pure Nim: stub+invoke), conformance_test extended, wallet_lez_test extended. payload.description: A lidl method over the manifest: for each Requirement return {requirement, status: met|missing|unknown, detail, remedy}. module → ask logos-core whether it is loaded (the discovery seam, coordination/discovery.nim); environment → the wallet adapter's chain reachability; authority → does the keystore identity recover to an owner / roster member (never reveal WHICH under an anonymous driver, inv 9); infra → RPC/store configured. Unknown is a first-class answer (null ladder, exo-1ec.5), never silently met. No network on the plugin side beyond the existing seams (inv 3). DONE WHEN a Safe intent on an instance without the RPC configured reports infra:missing with the remedy, and a non-owner reports authority:missing.

Actions: Install (a module requirement → the host install path, surfaced as a pointer until the Basecamp broker exists; the plugin never installs), Authorize (infra/authority remedies), Approve (existing contribute), Deny (a signed decline event folded into the intent view so the room sees who is out — named vs anonymous per driver). Launch-verified in the standalone runner; qmllint clean. DONE WHEN a proposer sees the peer's missing dependency on the card and the peer can deny.
payload.title: M3 Proposal card answers the five questions + per-participant readiness, with install / authorize / approve / deny actions

payload.description: Today F-20 provenance exists only on the signing path. Then a proof object: a log slice + signatures + hash links + the epoch it is scoped to, checkable by any epoch holder and by nobody else (inv 7). Decide and document whether a disclosable (out-of-room) proof is in scope — it is selective disclosure of a log slice, a new thing. Anonymous drivers name nothing (inv 9). Property test: proof verifies iff log unchanged; tamper → refuse.

payload.body: AppImage rebuilt from current HEAD a4cd9f7 (292MB). First 'make appimage' was stale (basecamp flake.lock pinned muster@bbe3c48, 69 commits behind) — repinned basecamp muster_module/muster_ui to main HEAD, rebuilt with max-jobs=1 (the max-jobs=4 default froze the machine via RAM+zram exhaustion). Headless verify all green: current surface incl action-manifest methods (readiness/flow/provenance/proof/authorization/decline), delivery variant linux-amd64, SDK-skew symbol absent, lp_token_save present, libsecp+libsodium co-located, offscreen load 0-errors. Remaining: interactive click-test (real display) + clean-machine run.

Two blockers found + fixed during test:
1) Click-test failed: 'Muster cannot be loaded — missing lez_core'. muster_module now declares dependency lez_core (LEZ wallet, landed 2026-09-14) but basecamp bake-in didn't bundle it. Fixed: added lez_core input (github:logos-blockchain/logos-execution-zone-module@549cf115) + lezCoreInstall/Portable into appDistributed's installedModules (mirrors delivery). Variant linux-amd64 confirmed. AppImage now 376MB (was 292; +lez_core runtime libs).
2) Build froze machine even at max-jobs=1: root cause = basecamp nix/main-ui.nix:50 + nix/app.nix:651 run 'cmake --build build' with -GNinja and NO -j → Ninja uses all 20 cores in ONE derivation, ignoring nix --cores. Fixed (LOCAL bake-in): bounded both to -j $NIX_BUILD_CORES. Rebuilt at --cores 3: memory plateaued ~6.4G avail, no freeze, exit 0.
Offscreen load clean (0 not-loadable, 0 dep errors). Awaiting interactive click-test.

BLOCKER: Muster hangs on spinner when clicked. All 3 modules load (lez_core/delivery/muster_module), but capability_module repeatedly fails: 'QObject::connect: No such signal ::eventResponse(QString,QVariantList)' every ~6s → async module calls never return → UI never renders.

ROOT CAUSE = ADR-013/exo-c6a SDK-coherence skew, resurfaced. muster_ui's QtRO/capability glue is built against a different logos-cpp-sdk generation than basecamp's host (fb88c7d5). muster's flake.locks are GITIGNORED and muster_ui's builder FLOATS cpp-sdk (no rev pin), so each git+file build re-resolves to a cpp-sdk that no longer matches basecamp. Timeline: basecamp flake.lock moved 2026-09-11 (86f0a12), one day AFTER last release v0.1.0-demo (09-10) which was built against basecamp's coherent pre-drift SDK. So last release renders; current-HEAD rebuild does not.

NOT release-ready as-is. Options: (A) re-pin muster ui+module flakes to basecamp's fb88c7d5 generation + rebuild [proper fix, docs warn it may break muster's build - the exo-c6a work]; (B) pin basecamp host back to pre-09-11 coherent SDK + rebuild [lower muster-build risk]; (C) defer release, keep v0.1.0-demo latest. Resource-limit fixes (ninja -j bound + max-jobs=1) DONE and working.

Fix-forward BLOCKED at builder level. Root cause pinpointed: eventResponse(QString,QVariantList) is a logos-cpp-sdk API present in 0.1.0, REMOVED in 0.2.0. basecamp host = 0.2.0 (fb88c7d5, bumped 2026-09-11 @86f0a12; was 0.1.0 e1d6bf20 before, = last-release generation). muster_module pinned to 0.1.0 (c3fa1b5a) → its Qt provider glue speaks the removed eventResponse bridge → events don't reach the 0.2.0 host → UI spins.

Bumping muster's SDK set to 0.2.0 (fb88c7d5) FAILS the module build: 'Error: --backend cdylib was removed from logos-qt-generator; this tool emits the CONSUMER glue, not the Qt-plugin (provider) glue.' The 0.2.0 generator restructured provider-glue emission; muster's builder fork (corpetty/logos-module-builder@c10a94cd) is built around 0.1.0's --backend cdylib. True fix-forward = port the builder fork to 0.2.0 (separate repo, substantial). module/flake.nix reverted to working 0.1.0.

TRACTABLE PATH (Option B): pin basecamp host back to 0.1.0 (e1d6bf20 gen) + pin muster_ui floating cpp-sdk to 0.1.0 → all coherent, reuses muster's known-good build, ships on the 0.1.0 host like v0.1.0-demo did.

payload.description:
source: utterance (Corey, 2026-09-23, follow-up to Jacek's exo-3a1)

Gap: exo-3a1 / invariant 10 commits a provenance record INTO every signing payload, but there is no way to take one signature out and hand it to someone as a complete, checkable account. What exists is split across surfaces and scoped to the whole room: coordinate_provenance (room-wide JSON fold, display-only), coordinate_proof (the whole room log, not one signature's slice), coordinate_authorization (the grant, not the lineage). The UI has no export/download at all.

Want: coordinate_signature_audit(intent_id[, signer]) -> one bundle (format muster.signature-audit.v1) holding: the signature + signing payload (profile, schema-id, environment/account/slot/expiry — inv 2); the effect and the re-derived materialization (inv 1); the committed provenance record; the parent-closed log slice for exactly the entries it names (reuse log/proof.nim); the driver manifest + disclosure rows; the other approvals and the submit/final external reads when present. Plus a pure verifier (coordinate_verify_signature_audit, and ideally a standalone CLI) that re-derives and refuses on mismatch. UI: a Download audit trail action on the card.

Constraints: anonymous drivers name no signer (inv 9); epoch-scoped so exporting is the member's selective disclosure of what they already hold, never more (inv 7, F-20); nothing new stored — the bundle is a reduction over log + keys (inv 4); deterministic encoding (inv 5).

Needs discuss-issue to become a typed spec (signing-path adjacent).
payload.title: Downloadable per-signature audit bundle: one self-verifying file that describes everything a signature covers

Wiring: propose publishes the intent context (driver environment, Safe/room account, intent-id slot, expiry = now + MUSTER_INTENT_TTL_S, default 7d); contribute refuses expired / no-context / unaccountable-input and publishes a same-key attestation over P with every in-app approval (pasted = unattested); the fold skips an approval whose attestations all fail to verify against its re-derived P; IntentView/card JSON carry committed + unattested, provenance/log provenance/activity carry the grade; logProvenance classes context/read/attest; submit refuses past expiry; reannounce carries context+reads to joiners. Bug found by the probes: provenance encoded the canonical INDEX beside the content id, so publishing any event shifted P under existing signatures — entries with a content id now encode only the id. Regression: 103/103 local tests+probes; coordinate_submit_anvil + safe_anvil_e2e pass on a fresh devnet (they are order-dependent on the Safe nonce — pre-existing); module .lgx builds.

AMENDED 2026-09-23 (operator-approved, after exo-ef1): s1/s2/s5/s6 for unattested + rejected approvals — every approval carries its grade; the verifier recomputes grades, accepts pasted approvals as unattested, refuses a claimed-committed approval without a verifying attestation; pasted never shown committed. Enabling design points approved with it: (1) non-derivable claims (threshold, stage, disclosure) signed by the exporting member's secp key; (2) submit/final events carry the tx hash (legacy '1' reads as unknown chain ref); (3) approvals link via parents (propose + the approvals their signer saw) so export refuses when lineage reaches an unreadable event, and the file labels its first epoch. Oracles amended to match (s1 adds pasted/rejected; s2 adds grade flip / strip / swap attestation + signed claims; s6 adds pasted-unattested; s7 report shows grades). validate_spec passes. Branch rebased onto fix/exo-ef1-live-provenance.

payload.description:
Found during the 2026-09-25 machine bring-up (exo-acc), while auditing mech-reduce-log.svg.

Evidence: module/src/log/log.nim:21-24 — Event is {parents, key, value}: content-addressed (eventId = hash-input 'muster.event.v1'), hash-linked, and sealed to the room under the epoch key (coordination/session.nim:93-96), but carries NO author signature. Authorship of several event kinds is a self-declared string:
- newMessageEvent(author, ts, body) — intent_events.nim:386 (chat messages)
- declineEvent(intentId, who) — intent_events.nim:270 (key intent/<id>/decline/<who>, value '1')
- materialShareEvent(..., who, ...) — intent_events.nim:283

Epoch sealing proves the sender held the room's epoch key (i.e. is SOME member), not WHICH member. So any member can publish a message, decline or share attributed to another member, and every view (activity, intent view 'declines', FlowView) will name the victim. Approvals are NOT affected: contributeEvent carries a signature the driver verifies against the contributor (and exo-ef1 grades attestation).

Why it matters: invariant 9 — 'Every driver is named — members know who approved, declined, or shared, inside the room' — holds for approvals only. The docs also overclaim: CLAUDE.md layout ('src/log/ signed hash-linked log'), README.md/module/README.md ('a signed hash-linked log'), log.nim's own header, and mech-reduce-log.svg ('EVERY EVENT SIGNED').

Options: (a) sign every event envelope with the author's Ed25519 encryption identity (already bound to the secp identity via binding.nim) and verify on ingest — the F-1 'signed log' the docs describe; (b) sign only the author-bearing kinds (message/decline/share) and verify author == signer in their folds; (c) keep unsigned and weaken the docs + inv-9 wording to 'as claimed by a room member'. (a) or (b) needs a red test first: a member publishes a decline naming another member; the fold must refuse it.
payload.title: Log events are not author-signed: any room member can forge another's message, decline, or material-share

payload.description:
Found by module/tools/action_corpus.nim (exo-3b8) generating every built (kind, effect) manifest for the action atlas (exo-661). Reported, not fixed:
1. safe.nim manifest: for a contract-call or delegatecall effect it still declares the counterparty 'payee' requirement bound to 'to' and the proposer 'amount' bound to 'value' — there 'to' is the token contract / MultiSend, not a payee. The payee/amount requirements should apply to a plain transfer only (no data).
2. safe.nim: the environment requirement is named 'chain:31337' while Driver.environment() returns 'eip155:31337' (CAIP-2). One name for one thing.
3. lez_frost.nim manifest: the 'lez:<account>' touch appears twice (the account, and again as the call's first account). Dedup.
4. lez_multisig.nim manifest: touches name only the chain and the proposal PDA, not the vault / recipient accounts the call writes.
Each shows verbatim in the atlas (generated = the code's truth), so fixing the driver fixes the atlas on regeneration (TEST_ARGS=--write module/tests/run-suite.sh action_corpus).
payload.title: Driver manifests the action atlas surfaced as imprecise (4)

payload.description:
Found while authoring the action atlas (exo-661, room actions), verified in code 2026-09-27. FS-9 / docs claim the store node (and anyone on the content topic — Waku topics are readable by any relay/subscriber) learns only a room's topic and timing, never its contents. In fact, in cleartext on the topic:
1. Join request (session.nim requestJoin): FrameJoinRequest & encodeLink(binding) — the joiner's Ed25519/X25519 encryption identity, its secp256k1 address and the binding signature. Anyone watching learns who is asking to join, and their chain address.
2. Admit (session.nim admit → epoch_crypto.nim admit/encodeGrant): one control frame per member of the new epoch, each = epoch (4 bytes) ‖ member count ‖ EVERY member's 64-byte identity ‖ the wrapped key. The full roster is published in the clear on every admit, N times.
3. Every data envelope (epoch_crypto.nim seal): a 4-byte epoch header in clear — membership-change timing is visible.
Also reported by the same pass (not yet verified): composer room names embed the verb and 6 hex digits of the peer's chat id.
Impact: room membership — who is in the room, and their secp addresses — is visible outside the room, against 'the conversation is the security boundary' and FS-9 as documented. Options: seal the grant's roster to each recipient (send only the wrapped key + a per-recipient envelope; members learn the roster from the sealed admit event already in the log), carry join requests as sealed-box invites to a member (like FrameInvite) instead of cleartext, and move the epoch index inside an AEAD-authenticated but key-selection-friendly scheme (e.g. try-keys or a keyed epoch tag). Red test first: a store-node-view probe that asserts no member identity bytes appear in any frame on the topic.
payload.title: The store node sees more than topic + timing: join requests, the full roster at every admit, the epoch on every frame

payload.description:
The A5 research (exo-889) declared candidate-family actions from primary sources and kept the registry's values where research contradicted them. Decide and correct contracts/families/registry.json (then scripts/check-family-registry.py --write-table):
- evm.erc7579-ownable expiry=optional: OwnableValidator.validateUserOp returns only 0/1 — owner signatures never expire; only a paymaster/hook can add a window (modulekit ERC7579ValidatorBase).
- mpc.threshold-ecdsa binding=explicit / ordering=sequence: both come from the target chain (implicit + utxo on Bitcoin). cggmp21 repo now hosts cggmp24, which has no refresh; only dkls23 does quorum change (unaudited, non-commercial).
- lez.public-witness sources link 'main' (stale, 47eba256, no shard_selectors/fee); the registry's 'signs' matches 'dev' — update the links.
- btc.miniscript-decay signs: 'spending path fixed in the signed bytes' holds only for tr (BIP-342 tapleaf hash); in wsh BIP-143 signs the whole witnessScript. Core's own decay example uses after(), not older() — refresh cannot help with after().
- zcash.frost-orchard expiry=forced vs ZIP-203 (nExpiryHeight=0 = no expiry; 40 blocks is a default). ZIP-312 says signers MUST check OR compute the SIGHASH. reddsa 0.6.0 (2026-09-25) removed the FROST ciphersuites (moving to the frost repo) — maturity drift.
- sol.squads-v4 notes: not every config change goes stale (AddSpendingLimit / RemoveSpendingLimit / SetRentCollector don't, config_transaction_execute.rs); 'program is immutable' unconfirmed.
- cosmos.x-auth-multisig bypasses=[]: an x/authz grant lets a grantee act without the k keys (x/authz/keeper/keeper.go) — a real bypass.
- sui.multisig binding/signs: TransactionExpiration ValidDuring carries a ChainIdentifier (transaction.rs L2429-2461); address-balance gas escapes ordering=objects; address aliases allow in-place key rotation (vs membershipChange=new-address).
- xrpl.signerlist: a multi-signed asfDisableMaster fails tecNEED_MASTER_KEY (AccountSet.cpp L305-329) — the bypass closes only with the master key holder; binding=none but no exposure field; NetworkID refused on ids ≤ 1024.
- dot.pallet-multisig: the migration that dropped multisigs is documented in rc-migrator/src/multisig.md, not the wiki source cited; ANY signatory can execute once k approvals are in, not only 'the final approver'.
- stellar.thresholds: bypasses omits the ed25519 signed-payload signer (CAP-40, SignatureChecker.cpp#L47) — its signature covers a fixed payload and is reusable; 'stop at exactly enough' → every signature must be used in envelope order before weight reaches threshold (txBAD_AUTH_EXTRA); Soroban address-credential signatures have a forced signatureExpirationLedger.

payload.description:
Found by the action-atlas authoring pass (exo-661), reproduced 2026-09-27. coordination/intents.nim reduceIntents dedups contributions by the contributor NAME in the event key (intent/<id>/sig/<who>/<round>), and Collection.submit (drivers/driver.nim) counts every contribution the driver accepts — verifyContribution accepts a valid signature from ANY eligible signer. Nothing checks that <who> is the signer. So one valid signature published under two names counts twice.
Repro (pure fold): threshold driver, roster [A,B,C], k=2; events = propose, contributeEvent(id,'A', sigA), contributeEvent(id,'B', sigA) → intentState = executable with ONE signer. An unattested (pasted) approval counts, so no attestation is needed; any member holding the epoch key can publish raw events.
Impact: for room policies the fold IS the outcome — a single member can complete a threshold statement, an invoke action (coordinate_execute runs it when executable) or an add-driver governance proposal (roomDriverKinds admits the kind). Chain settlements (Safe, Bitcoin, LEZ) re-count distinct signers on chain, so nothing wrong settles on chain, but the room shows 'executable'.
Fix: the fold must identify the signer (driver.identifyContributor over the intent's materialization) and dedup by the IDENTIFIED signer per round, rejecting a contribution whose key names someone other than its signer. Red test first: the repro above must fold to 'collecting'; plus a probe (invariant 6 / conformance: a driver's collection counts distinct eligible signers).
payload.title: The room fold counts one signer twice: a k-of-n room decision can be completed by one member

payload.description: Left out of exo-a5a (#164). approvalGrades (coordination/attest.nim) grades every sig event whose name matches its identified signer — or, when the driver can identify NO signer for the bytes (identifyContributor = ''), takes it at its name. A garbage signature published under a real member's name therefore identifies as '' → falls back to the name → graded 'unattested' → the card's M of N and the activity feed count it as an approval, although the fold never counts it (verifyContribution rejects it). Display only: the lifecycle state is right. Fix: grade such a contribution 'rejected' — needs verifyContribution in the view, which is stateful for multi-round drivers (FROST round 2 depends on round-1 nonces), so either expose the fold's accepted set to the views or add a stateless 'plausible signer' hook. Test: a garbage sig under member B's name must not raise the card's approval count.
payload.title: Views count an invalid signature under a real name as an approver (display only)

payload.description:
Found reading the client end to end for docs/runbooks/client-tour.md (2026-09-28). Each was read from the code; none is yet confirmed on screen. Split into their own pebbles as they get picked up.
1. Approve stays visible after you approve: approvedByMe is never set (ui/src/qml/Room.qml:387); the card offers Approve again.
2. The Accounts list goes stale: coordinate_accounts reloads only on join or your own disclose (ui/src/muster_ui_backend.cpp:214, :761), not on the 1 s tick — another member's disclosure, the LEZ create pump's, or a finished FROST ceremony's does not appear until you re-enter the room.
3. A Bitcoin spend and a lez-call carry no value/to, so the card shows "Proposed a payment" with no amount or outputs; LEZ multisig and add-driver cards read "Proposed a statement" (MusterCard.qml heading/effect lines).
4. Room history mislabels non-Safe effects as "a payment: 0 → " and says "Submitted on-chain — the Safe execTransaction was sent through the RPC" / "the payment landed" for every family, including Run the action (module/src/coordination/intents.nim:312-314, :379-385).
5. A settle still pending after ~4 s is never re-checked for Safe or Bitcoin (muster_module.nim coordinate_submit ~:1879-1886; only LEZ has a pump), so it can sit at "Submitted — awaiting finality".
6. A refused Run the action returns {executed:false} with no error (muster_module.nim:2260-2261), so the UI shows "Running…" (Room.qml:1168) instead of the refusal.
7. attestation-mismatch is not in the backend's not-ok list (muster_ui_backend.cpp:400-403): such an approval gives no warning.
8. coordinate_request_join's "waiting-for-room-key" (and "not-joined") is only logged (muster_ui_backend.cpp:314, :349); nothing tells the user their ask is waiting.
9. The Room header shows the raw topic ("Room · %1", Room.qml:646), not the session title Home uses (Main.qml roomLabels); titles are session-only.
10. No UI discloses a btc.p2wsh-sortedmulti / btc.tapscript-multi-a account, and no surface shows a member's compressed secp key (keystore btcPubKey) — the two Bitcoin multisig families can be driven only headless.
11. Nothing in the app mints a LEZ token or funds a LEZ multisig vault or a LEZ FROST group account, so their settle is expected to be rejected on the testnet.
12. The Bitcoin recipient placeholder reads "recipient (0x…)" (Room.qml:1718).
13. Declines render as clipped ids with no alias ("%1 declined: …", MusterCard.qml:1167); approval slots never name approvers (card.approvers is never supplied).
14. infra/fleets/README.md:37-39 describes a default isolated node and a kDefaultDeliveryPreset that no longer exist; the handoff's "regtest.sh start" suggests a subcommand that isn't one; MUSTER_RPC is documented (devnet.sh, transaction-lifecycle-demo.md) but never read.

payload.description: A room action where one member fronted a bill and the others each owe a share. The room agrees who owes what (each person named signs the split with their room key); each then pays their own share from their own wallet — muster builds the payment from the agreed split and refuses anything else (inv 1); the creditor's client confirms each payment from its own chain read; the split is final when every share is confirmed. A new coordination shape (locus 'each': no shared account), a family per rail (evm.split built first, lez.split — the private rail — next). Design: docs/design/split-the-bill.md.

payload.description: Found while fixing exo-b96 (verified 2026-09-28). reduceIntents (module/src/coordination/intents.nim) dedups contributions by (who, key round) but Collection.submit (drivers/driver.nim) verifies each at the collection's CURRENT round, not the key's. The room FrostDriver (drivers/frost.nim) is round-agnostic by design, relying on the core to make both rounds reach k. So member A's one Ed25519 signature published as contributeEvent(id, A, sig, round=1..4) makes a 2-of-3 room-FROST intent EXECUTABLE alone: A/1 and A/2 close round 1, A/3 and A/4 close round 2. (btc/lez FROST refuse it: their contributions embed their round.) Fix direction: in the fold, count a contribution only toward its own key round (skip when its round != the collection's current round), and add a red test first. The view (approvalGrades, which verifies at the key round since exo-b96) would then agree with the fold for round-agnostic drivers too.

payload.description:
source: utterance

S9 exo-a90.10: split-the-bill typed spec. Split the bill (docs/design/split-the-bill.md, epic exo-a90): one member fronted a bill; the room agrees who owes what — each debtor signs their own share with their room key — then each pays their own share from their own wallet, and the creditor's client confirms each payment from its own read; the split is final when every share is confirmed. Two families: evm.split (public payments) and lez.split (the private split: shielded payee, private rail, every share a distinct amount, the creditor confirms by scan). The typed spec fixes the split's guarantees with an acceptance oracle each: (1) the payment is derived from the agreed effect, never supplied (invariant 1); (2) parts converge under reorder and duplication (invariant 4); (3) only the named party records 'settled' for its part and only the counterparty records 'confirmed' (invariant 9); (4) a split's finality is its parts' — a bare submit or final never finalizes a parts intent; (5) one on-chain reference or private note settles at most one part; (6) the private split: shares pairwise distinct, private rail only, a part confirmed only by the creditor's own scan finding a note of exactly that share.

payload.description: Found while fixing exo-e42 (verified 2026-09-28). reduceIntents (module/src/coordination/intents.nim, pass 2) checks attribution (signedByNamed), then dedups by (who, round), and only then lets Collection.submit verify. signedByNamed passes whenever the driver cannot name a signer, which is also what it says of an invalid contribution. So an epoch-key holder's junk under A's name that sorts ahead of A's real signature in canonical order takes A's slot, and A's real signature is dropped as a duplicate. The publisher can grind the junk bytes until it sorts first. approvalGrades (coordination/attest.nim) verifies BEFORE dedup (exo-b96), so the views still count A: the fold and the card disagree. Repro: threshold k=2 roster {a,b}; events = policy+propose, A's real sig, junk hex('00'*64 etc., chosen so eventId(junk) < eventId(realA)) under A's name, B's real sig. Result: intentState = collecting, reduceIntentViews approvals = 2. Fix direction: in the fold, drop a contribution the driver does not verify (expectMaterialization + verifyContribution at its round) BEFORE dedup, like approvalGrades; red test first in view_counts_fold_test (append-only).

payload.description: Found while fixing exo-c00 (verified 2026-09-28). A live approval lists every sig event of its intent as a parent (liveContribute / liveFrostContribute / vote.nim, exo-403: 'link the approval to every approval its signer has seen'). The audit export carries only the lineage (provenance closure) and the GRADED approvals, and verifyAudit refuses any carried event whose parent the file lacks ('approval by X links an entry the file does not carry'). So any sig event the fold does not count, published before an honest member approves, makes that intent's audit file unverifiable. Examples: junk under any name (even the publisher's own), a non-member's signature, a key under a round the collection never reached, or a second copy of a valid signature ground to sort first so it becomes the counted event. Any epoch-key holder can do this to any intent. Repro: audit_room fixture, threshold; alice approves; bob publishes contributeEvent(id, <any name>, junk); bob approves; exportAudit ok, verifyAudit refuses. Directions to weigh: (a) approvals link only the counted approvals (approvalGrades' g.sig) — fragile, because the counted event under a key can change as events arrive; (b) the file carries the parent closure of everything it carries in a separate 'linked' section the verifier checks, not grades — an audit format change under derived-exo-403 (probes: completeness, tamper, determinism). Red test first.
payload.title: Audit: a carried approval that links an uncounted contribution makes the file unverifiable

payload.description: Found while fixing exo-96d (verified 2026-09-28). The audit file is parent-closed, and since exo-96d the export refuses (naming the link) rather than hand over a file its verifier refuses. But it carries some events whose parents anyone holding the epoch key chooses, and one parent outside the intent's record makes the export refuse. Two ways: (1) every attestation event under an approval's key is carried, so a bogus attestation parented on a room message blocks the export ('the attestation of X's approval links message/…, an entry outside this intent's record'); (2) a valid copy of a member's signature (same key and value) parented on a room message and ground to sort first becomes the counted event, which the file carries as the approval ('approval by X links message/…'). Repro: audit_room fixture, threshold; alice and bob approve; bob posts a message and publishes attestEvent(id, <alice's name>, 1, junk, parents=@[message id]), or a copy Event(parents=@[message id], key/value = alice's sig) that sorts first; exportAudit refuses. Carrying the message would pad the file with room content (s1 over-disclosure), so closure alone cannot fix it. Directions: carry only the attestations a grade needs (one verifying one for committed; for rejected, one whose parents the record holds), and pick as an approval's carried signature a copy whose parents the record holds (every valid copy under a key is the same approval), keeping the others as alternates only when something links them. Red test first (audit_linked_test or a new file).
payload.title: Audit: an event with attacker-chosen parents outside the intent blocks the export

payload.body:
Fixed.
(1) Approvals link only the proposal and the approvals the fold counts: approvalParents (attest.nim), used by liveContribute, liveFrostContribute and castVote/receipts.
(2) The audit file carries, per approval, any other valid copy of its signature under the same key that the carried events link ('alternates', absent when none, so v1 bytes are unchanged). This covers a copy that sorts ahead of the original and becomes the counted event. The verifier checks each copy: same key, signed by the named contributor, linked, in order. An approval hidden as another's copy, or a padded copy, is refused even when the exporter signs the file.
(3) The export checks closure itself and refuses, naming the link, instead of emitting a file its verifier refuses (e.g. an approval from an older client that linked junk).
Residual, filed as exo-093: an attestation, or a counted copy, whose attacker-chosen parents lie outside the intent now gets a named refusal, but it still blocks the export.

payload.description: Found while rebasing exo-e42 onto main (2026-09-28). Main's collection now runs on the proposal's own policy, describeFor(driver, effect) (exo-a90.2): a family can declare its threshold, and in principle its rounds, per proposal. approvalGrades (coordination/attest.nim, exo-e42) decides which rounds the collection has reached from drv.describe(), the family's one policy. A driver whose per-proposal rounds or threshold differ from describe() gets grades that disagree with the fold. For example, describe() says 1 round and describeFor says 2: a round-2 approval the fold counts gets no grade, so the card's 'this round' count and the audit omit it. No shipped driver does this today (split is single-round), so this is latent. Fix: read describeFor(drv, effect) in approvalGrades. Red test first in view_counts_fold_test (append-only).
payload.title: approvalGrades reads describe() while the fold's collection reads describeFor(effect)

On ef16319, before #172 merged, a split's card counted the creditor's agreement and a room member's who is not a debtor; split_driver_test checks only the fold state. Add split scenarios (a debtor + the creditor + a non-debtor member; every debtor + the non-debtor) so every surface stays held to the fold for this family.

payload.description: Found 2026-09-29 while merging #174: the same binary failed 13 of 20 runs. The oracle (leave-one-out: a (who, round) is counted iff removing it lowers the fold's total) exposes the exo-e42 fold quirk. Removing a round-1 contribution leaves round 1 short, and the round-1 payload replayed under key round 2 can then fill it, but only when it sorts before host 0's partial. FROST nonces come from urandom, so that order is random per run. The test landed on main via #172. Fix: an incremental oracle that feeds the fold its contributions one at a time, in its own processing order (key round, then canonical order), and keeps each one that raises the total. The verdicts stay the fold's, and the result is deterministic.
payload.title: view_counts_fold_test is flaky (~50%) in its btc FROST scenario

The effect carries base units (signed); decimals/symbol are display-only chain reads, never signed. payload.description: Left after exo-093 (2026-09-28). exo-093 made the intent's record closed: the lineage, plus the copies of its approvals whose parents lie in the record. An attestation counts only if it links nothing but copies of its own approval there; the copy that stands for an approval is one inside the record. Two narrow cases still end in a NAMED export refusal (never an unverifiable file): (1) multi-round only (the room FROST scaffold is the one auditable multi-round family). The admitted-attestation rule uses the copies under every round the proposal runs, but the export carries copies only for GRADED (reached) keys. So an attacker-built chain (a copy under an unreached round's key, then a copy of an approval parented on it, then a forged attestation parented on that) is admitted by the fold but its parent cannot be carried. Fixing it needs the admitted set computed over graded keys, which depends on grades through reach, a fixpoint. (2) A fake submit/final parented outside the record, when no honest one exists: the fold still counts it (stage submitted/final) and the file cannot carry it. Settlement events are unauthenticated anyway (external reads), so the fix belongs with authenticating or ignoring them in the fold, activity, logProvenance and flow alike.
payload.title: Audit: two narrow ways an out-of-record event still blocks the export

payload.description: Seen 2026-09-28: tests/probes/probe_return_marshalling_host.nim builds its C++ host harness under getTempDir()/muster_exo526_host (line 99). Two run-suite.sh runs at once, from different worktrees or sessions, share that directory, and one fails with 'ar rcs … failed' (reported inconclusive and FAIL). Rerun alone, it passes. Fix: a per-run directory (e.g. under the suite's OUT, or a mkdtemp).
payload.title: probe_return_marshalling_host builds into a fixed /tmp path, so concurrent suite runs collide

payload.body:
Fixed. The intent's record is closed: its lineage, plus the copies of its approvals whose parents all lie in the record.
- An attestation belongs to the intent only if it links nothing but copies of its own approval there. That rule applies in the fold's gate, the grades, the FROST signer set, logProvenance and the export: a forged attestation parented on a room message or on junk neither rejects the approval nor rides in the audit.
- The copy that stands for an approval (g.sig) is the first inside the record, so honest approvals link it and the export carries it. A copy parented outside the intent stands for nothing.
- The export carries only the record, plus a settlement entry whose parents it holds.
Residuals, filed as exo-dc6: multi-round chains through an unreached round's key, and a fake settlement parented outside with no honest one. Both end in a named refusal.

Done. Driver: erc20:<0x token> in one spelling (split_driver_test §10). Seam: transfer(payTo, share) on the token via the adapter's ERC-20 path, client-side signed; the creditor confirms from the receipt's Transfer log — that token, exactly the share, to payTo (wallet/erc20_logs + evm_rpc.rpcReceiptLogs; erc20_logs_test). e2e split_erc20_anvil_e2e: both decoys refused, +0.6 MTD exact, final on all three. Hosted: coordinate_token_info (new lidl; symbol/decimals display-only, cached, via your RPC), the propose shares object takes asset, the card carries symbol/decimals/token; history reads '0.9 MTD' (split_driver_test §11). UI verified on display (Xvfb): the composer's token field + lookup + preview in MTD, the card 'Paid in MTD — the token at 0x5fbdb231…', Bob paid from the UI, Alice +0.45 MTD, final on both, history named. Atlas/registry/design doc §4.8/CLAUDE.md updated.
Already fixed on main by 3baebde ('the host-marshalling probe builds in its own directory per run'), which landed in parallel with this report. Seen after rebasing onto 607d441.

payload.description: Found while fixing exo-dc6 (verified 2026-09-29). The room FROST scaffold (drivers/frost.nim, policy 'frost', a selectable room policy via driverForKind) names contributors 'frost:<hex of the Ed25519 key>' (identifyContributor). Two name-based helpers know only 'ed:', '0x' and compressed secp keys: (1) attest.nim verifyAttestation. liveContribute's in-app path makes an Ed25519 attestation over P, then checks it with verifyAttestation(who, …), which returns false for 'frost:…', so it returns 'attestation-mismatch' and publishes nothing. The hosted module approves through liveContribute (muster_module.nim ~1580), so an in-app Approve on a room-FROST intent never lands. (2) audit.nim signedBy returns false for 'frost:…', so verifyAudit refuses any room-FROST audit file that carries an approval ('is not signed by'). No test caught either: the FROST tests publish raw contributeEvent without attestations or audits. Repro: newFrostDriver(roster alice/bob enc ed, 2); liveProposeIntent 'frost'; liveContribute(…, '', …) returns 'attestation-mismatch'. Fix direction: treat 'frost:<hex>' as an Ed25519 key in both helpers (and check myContributorNames / approvedByMe agree); red test first via the live path + audit.
payload.title: Room FROST: in-app Approve is refused (attestation-mismatch), and no room-FROST audit verifies — frost:<hex> names are unknown to verifyAttestation and signedBy

payload.body:
Fixed.
(1) Multi-round: a copy may link only record copies of its own round or earlier ones (closedWithin). Honest copies do. So the record of rounds up to r never depends on a later round, and what it holds for a reached round the file can carry. A chain through a copy under a round not yet reached is no part of the record.
(2) Settlement: the first attempt (the fold and every view ignore a submit/final parented outside the lineage) broke flow_test: a submit parented on an approval behind a membership admit dropped out of the flow view. A settlement entry's parents say nothing about whether it is true. So instead a settlement entry is a leaf of the audit file: carried with its content id checked, never its ancestry, in the export and the verifier alike. The fold and the views are unchanged.
Tested with a two-round threshold variant: room-FROST audits cannot verify at all until exo-75c (frost:<hex> names unknown to verifyAttestation / signedBy).

Fixed. verifyAttestation and the audit's signedBy treat 'frost:<hex>' as the Ed25519 key it names, as they do 'ed:<hex>'. An in-app Approve of a room-FROST intent now lands committed, and a room-FROST audit verifies. The other name-based helpers (contacts, myContributorNames, the hosted module's name handling) already knew 'frost:'. frost_room_live_test drives the scaffold through the live path; each half is red without its own fix.

payload.description: Main.qml's homeActions marks a room 'needs' only when the room's LAST intent is executable; it never asks what waits on THIS member. Seen on display 2026-09-29 (exo-770): B's Home said 'Nothing waiting on you' while a split proposed on B's behalf waited on B's own Agree. The same holds for a debtor who has not agreed or paid, and for a Safe owner who has not approved. Derive 'needs' per intent from the coordinate_intents projection (approvedByMe, split.iAmCreditor && !creditorAgreed, parts[].mine && !settled, ...) — the card already knows each of these.
payload.title: Home: 'waiting on you' should mean you — a split waiting on your agreement or payment

payload.description: readiness.nim's authority arm has no case for the split driver's 'split-party' requirement (drivers/split.nim manifest, rpContributor), so the card's 'What this needs' shows '? authority: split-party — unrecognized authority requirement' on every split (seen on display 2026-09-29). Grade it for THIS instance: met when my room identity is a debtor or the creditor the effect names, missing otherwise — never who else is (inv 9). Pre-existing since 1a2ba54 (exo-a90).
payload.title: Readiness grades a split's authority requirement (split-party) as unknown

payload.body:
Built on feat/split-proposer (2026-09-29), per the chosen fix 'Sign proposals instead':
- A split's creditor is a party. Threshold = debtors + 1, and the creditor's own proposal agrees then (the agreesByProposing seam). Every proposal publishes a signed intent/<id>/proposer/<who> claim (IntentView.proposers).
- coordinate_propose_split {creditor} proposes on a member's behalf, paid at their latest signed address-share (sharedAddressOf). The creditor's client refuses a payTo it does not hold (payto-not-mine).
- UI: 'Who paid the bill?', the creditor's Agree, and 'Proposed by X on Y's behalf'.
- Verified: the full suite (168); grade-specs exo-a90 6/6; the live split-self-test.sh, normal (17s) and SPLIT_ON_BEHALF=1 (24s, B gained exactly A's share). The on-behalf card and composer were checked on Xvfb, and so was proposing from the UI.
- Filed along the way: exo-ed5 and exo-272.

payload.description:
A split's agreement binds to its intent context's expiry: DefaultIntentTtl, 7 days from propose (module/src/coordination/live.nim:37; the host reads MUSTER_INTENT_TTL_S). After it, liveSettlePartSend refuses with "expired" (coordination/parts.nim:141). That refusal is right (invariant 2: an agreement is bounded), but nothing gets the room out:
- Re-proposing the identical split gives the SAME intent id (intentIdFor(effect, policy)). The second context event does not renew it: intentContext takes the first context in canonical order (coordination/attest.nim:98), so the expiry may stay the old one, and the old agreements still count.
- There is no withdraw, and no re-propose with a fresh expiry.
- Check whether the card and Home show the split as expired, or leave it looking payable.
- A settle-up can still cover an expired split's parts: coverRefusal (coordination/covers.nim) checks the state, not the expiry. That revives the agreement without anyone deciding to.

Needs a decision, then code. Options:
(a) An expired, unfinished split shows as expired and can be re-proposed as a NEW intent (e.g. the expiry or a salt in the id), with fresh agreements.
(b) The same parties renew it with fresh agreements under a new context.
Either way, the cover check should refuse an expired split's parts, or the decision should record why not.

Red-first test: propose → agree → clock past expiry → pay refused "expired" → the chosen path → agree → pay → final.
payload.title: An expired split strands its unpaid shares — no way to renew or re-propose

payload.description:
coveringIntent (module/src/coordination/covers.nim:56) treats any settle-up in executable/submitted/settling/final as covering its parts, whatever its expiry. Once an agreed settle-up passes its expiry unpaid, three refusals hold at once:
1. its own net parts are refused "expired" (coordination/parts.nim:141);
2. the covered split parts are refused "covered-by-settle-up" (parts.nim:136);
3. a new settle-up cannot cover them, because coverRefusal says they are "already being settled by another agreed intent".

Those shares can never be paid.

Two cases:
- Nothing paid: an expired settle-up should release its covers, so the split parts are payable directly again or can be re-netted.
- Partly paid (submitted/settling, then expired): the paid net transfers are real money. Falling back to the original split parts would double-pay, so this needs a design decision; balance conservation across what was already paid is the constraint.

Red-first test in settle_up_live_test's shape: agree a settle-up, pass its expiry with nothing paid, then pay a covered split part directly (today: covered-by-settle-up). Design: docs/design/split-the-bill.md §4.11.
payload.title: An expired settle-up locks the shares it covers forever

payload.description:
Settle-up nets only one chain + asset: openParts(events, driverFor, chain, asset) in coordination/settle_up.nim, and the effect names one chain and asset. A room with both ETH and USDC splits needs two settle-ups.

Netting across assets needs a rate for each pair. That is an external read, like the fiat quote (exo-3a4): recorded before anyone agrees (invariant 10), signed in the materialization, and converted exactly, never rounded.

Decide whether it is worth it. If so, reuse the quote machinery (fiatQuote / readEvent) and keep conservation per asset checkable. The private split stays out (never netted).
payload.title: Settle up across assets (net ETH and a token, or two chains, at a recorded rate)

contracts/specs/derived-exo-a90.spec.json was graded 6/6 before exo-770 (proposer != creditor), exo-3a4 (fiat) and exo-3c6 (settle-up) landed. Its clauses still say "every named debtor" agrees; the creditor now agrees too.

Missing oracles:
- **Settle-up conservation:** every member's net balance is unchanged by replacing the covered parts with the net transfers.
- **The cover check:** a cover says exactly what its split says; the split is agreed and unpaid, and not already covered.
- **Settle-up payment:** a covered part is paid only through the settle-up, and is marked received only once the settle-up is final.
- **The fiat conversion:** the total IS the quote's exact conversion, and the quote reaches the signed bytes only as a recorded read (invariant 10).
- **The creditor agrees:** a split is payable only once its creditor agrees (payto-not-mine).
- **btc.split:** the creditor confirms an output of exactly the share at depth.

Run through the discuss-issue skill: the human approves the restatement, then signs off each oracle. Catastrophic, like the original. Grade with scripts/grade-specs.sh exo-a90.

Invariant 2 requires a signature to be worthless anywhere else. For the private split (lez.split), the payment is a LEZ privacy-preserving transaction built by lez_core. It is unverified whether that transaction commits to the zone or chain id, which would make it unreplayable on another zone. This is noted as open in CLAUDE.md and docs/labbook/lez-wallet-scan-and-proving.md.

payload.body: Root cause (from B's ui-host lines in the systemd journal): B's autopilot made its ONE agree attempt at 18:25:09 and coordinate_contribute answered 'no-context' — the split was in B's view but its signing context (the separate intent/<id>/context event the proposer publishes after the propose) had not arrived yet; over the fleet's ~1s store poll the two can land in different ticks. Refusing is right (inv 2); the autopilot never retried (agreeing was one-shot, paying already retried). Fix (branch fix/split-autopilot-agree-retry): the debtor and creditor agree branches retry every 2s up to 60s on a transient refusal (no-context / unknown-intent / unaccountable-input), logging each retry; the room's approval banner now explains no-context and unaccountable-input instead of printing the code. Proven: a throwaway build forcing the first agree to see no-context retried and went final in 22s; 20/20 green live runs (10 at the 1s poll, 10 at 200ms). Also documented QT_FORCE_STDERR_LOGGING=1 (backend lines into self-test logs; else they go to journald).

payload.description: The hosted split pump drops a pending payment after the seam's payDeadlineS ('timed out: the payment never landed', module/nim-lib/muster_module.nim splitPump). From then on the in-flight guard (exo-a90.18, liveSettlePartSend inFlight) no longer holds that part back, and the log still shows it unpaid, so Pay sends it again. If the first payment still lands (a low-fee Bitcoin transaction, a stuck EVM nonce), the share is paid twice. Options: keep a timed-out payment as 'maybe in flight' and ask the chain before paying again (EVM: the nonce / receipt by hash; BTC: the txid in mempool or chain; LEZ: the resolved tx), or refuse to re-pay a part whose earlier payment is still unresolved, naming it. Red-first: a fake seam whose payment lands after the deadline.

payload.body: Done on test/split-variants (stacked on #188): fiat in BTC/token/private split (split_fiat_test §5-7); settle-up in a token (settle_up_erc20_anvil_e2e) and in BTC (settle_up_btc_regtest_e2e). Found + fixed: a part in flight could be paid twice (liveSettlePartSend inFlight → 'paying'); a second BTC payment reused the first's mempool-spent coin, refused as an underpaying RBF replacement on Core 31 (spendableUtxosOf). Follow-up filed: exo-a90.23 (timed-out payment re-payable).

Answered from LEZ source at v0.2.4 (testnet) and v0.2.2 (muster's pin): a privacy-preserving tx names no zone/chain id (message.rs:21), but every nullifier's commitment-set root must be in the zone's own root_history (state/mod.rs:357-372). The private split's payment spends the debtor's own private account, so it lands only on its zone; exposure = a fork/replica sharing the history, or a genesis-root-only tx with matching public nonces (never the split). Labbook §10; atlas lez.split claims updated (unverified entry removed).

payload.description:
Found by reading the split/settle-up UI end to end for docs/runbooks/client-tour.md (exo-4a2), 2026-09-29. Each is listed in the tour's known rough edges; none is fixed yet.

1. Reports need the room on screen: a debtor's settled report and the creditor's confirmation run only while that room is the active session (module/nim-lib/muster_module.nim ~1100, ~1136); pending payments live only in memory, so quitting before a payment lands loses its report. Past the 600 s EVM/BTC deadline 'Pay my share' comes back, which invites a second payment (check against exo-a90.18 on test/split-variants).
2. The rail row shows '%1 needed' beside the split buttons (Room.qml ~1672), though every named party must agree.
3. A Bitcoin split card offers 'Sign outside muster (PSBT)' (isBtcIntent matches any btc- policy, Room.qml ~339/1151), which answers 'No PSBT — no-outside-format'.
4. A settle-up card offers 'Paste a signature instead' (Room.qml ~1085: settle-ups have no split field).
5. After paying in a token, the note prints 'erc20:0x…' instead of the symbol (Room.qml ~1066/1070).
6. Once a settle-up is final, its covered shares read '✓ received outside muster' (MusterCard.qml ~302).
7. Split and settle-up errors show two lines (Room.qml ~2442 and ~2560); a settle-up error reads 'The split was not proposed'; the last result never clears.
8. The verify box's 'shown' row is blank on a split card (MusterCard.qml ~99–108).
9. 'Split (Bitcoin)' with no Bitcoin node reports no-rpc and tells the user to check Settings → RPC (module ~1580, Room.qml ~1725); no-lez-wallet shows as a raw slug (~1727).
10. A failed rail choice leaves the previous split policy in force, so an ETH split can be proposed without the user noticing.
11. The 'Ask the room' detour through Payment selects 'safe'; with no disclosed Safe an error line appears and stays when back in Split.
12. No screen shows a member's own Bitcoin payer address (only the key).

payload.description:
Seen on a display (exo-a90.19): two runners relaunched into a room with ~100 messages came back showing the room as it was ~5 minutes earlier. The settle-up and its payments were missing, and B's card offered 'Pay my share' for a share the settle-up had already paid. The cover check reads the log, so on that stale view it would not stop a second payment.

Cause: module/src/transport/delivery.nim fireCatchup. The first DeepCatchupTicks (3) store queries use paginationForward:true, paginationLimit:50 and no paginationCursor, so each returns the same OLDEST 50 messages. After that, every query is windowed to the last MUSTER_CATCHUP_LOOKBACK_MS (60s). Anything between the 50th message and the last minute is never fetched. Nothing is persisted in the user dir either (12K), so a restart relies entirely on this catch-up.

Fix: follow the store's paginationCursor. The delivery module's storeQuery echoes requestId and returns paginationCursor (delivery_module_plugin.h). Deep-page each topic on the peer that issued the cursor until a page comes back without one, then switch to the window. Unit-test the pagination state without a node; check it live by relaunching a runner into the display room.

payload.description:
Logos Testnet v0.3 launched 2026-09-30 (https://blog.logos.co/article/logos-testnet-v03-live). Its rolling upgrade of the logos.test fleet took every node down for a day, and with it every two-instance self-test (diagnosed 2026-09-30; muster's delivery_module v0.2.0 client still worked through the first upgraded node). What v0.3 changes for muster:

- Delivery: logos-delivery-module v0.3.0 (2026-09-30, liblogosdelivery v0.39.0). messageReceived gains a source arg (live|history); store catch-up (backfill) is on by default; QUIC on UDP at the TCP port; module-builder 0.3.1.
- RLN: on for the logos.test preset. A v0.3 node there needs liblogos_rln_module >= 0.10.0 + liblogos_lez_rln_module >= 4.2.1 and an ACTIVE membership before start passes; the RLN module makes the node's own LEZ wallet and registers once its payer holds >= 2e8 native LEZ testnet. Proof validation turns on ~2 weeks after launch (~2026-10-14), after which v0.2 clients cannot publish on logos.test.
- logos.dev is now cluster 3 with RLN off; v0.2.0 resolves the preset to cluster 2, which is why logos.dev peers drop muster at the metadata handshake.
- LEZ: v0.3 changes the program state model (incremental diffs; existing programs must be updated), public transactions carry fees, and the testnet may be reset.

Sources: delivery v0.3.0 release notes; docs/pages/{rln,networks,run-node}.md at v0.3.0 in logos-co/logos-delivery-module.

payload.description:
Basecamp 0.3.1's default catalog ships an EVM key stack: keystore_module (scrypt vaults, BIP39/32, secp256k1; the only module holding EVM key material), evm_signer_ui (the approval surface, the human types the vault password), tx_sender_module (the device's one nonce ledger + broadcast). Moving muster's secp256k1 authorization signing onto it puts the key where the platform keeps keys, and the human approval where the platform shows it, instead of muster's FileKeystore stopgap (FS-4).

What changes for muster (atlas: https://github.com/corpetty/logos-module-atlas/blob/main/stacks/evm-wallet.md, https://github.com/corpetty/logos-module-atlas/blob/main/stacks/key-custody.md, https://github.com/corpetty/logos-module-atlas/blob/main/guides/calling-official-modules.md#72-sketch-adding-keystore_module-evm):
- Signing becomes asynchronous and human-approved: request_approval -> {handle, receipt} -> a human approves in evm_signer_ui -> approval_status -> fetch_result -> ack_result. No synchronous sign() exists; the Keystore seam's sign() cannot be a straight call.
- muster can READ accounts (list_accounts / get_labels / get_account_wallets are ungated) and REQUEST signatures (Tier B: any plainly named module), never create, import or export keys (Tier D, custodian only; hand off with the evm.accounts.manage intent).
- Attribution is the runtime's: keystore reads current_caller(); only a plain Module{name} may request. Whether a protocol-0.2 Nim caller (muster_module over lp_client_create(..., "muster_module")) is attributed as Module{muster_module} is UNVERIFIED and gates everything else -> K1.
- Transactions go through tx_sender_module (prepare -> send -> evm.signing.approve -> poll send_status, the poll broadcasts); Safe owner signatures are typed_data legs the keystore renders field by field (not opaque digests).
- Platform posture: Basecamp 0.3.1 runs --access-policy off by default and keystore configure() is ungated; muster must never call configure.

Pinned: keystore_module 0.1.0 = logos-co/logos-evm-keystore-module@2318c679 (catalog tag keystore_module-v0.1.0).
payload.title: The official keystore_module as muster's EVM key backend (Basecamp 0.3.1 evm-wallet stack)

payload.description:
Accept (an integration test before implementation, per the working agreements):
1. keystore_module (logos-evm-keystore-module@2318c679) rides the standalone runner's module set and muster_module's metadata.json dependencies.
2. A pure grader (module/src/wallet/keystore_status.nim, unit-tested in tests/keystore_status_test.nim) turns keystore replies into one status row {key:"keystore", level, detail, remedy?, identity:{kind,identity}, approvers, accounts:[{address,label,wallet}]}. ok ONLY when caller_identity says kind=module and identity=muster_module and some approver is named; any other kind (host, derived, operator, unknown) or another module's name is an error that says every request would be refused ("not authorized"); no approvers is a warn (nothing could ever settle); an unreachable or unparseable keystore is down. Nothing unread reads as ok.
3. muster.lidl gains keystore_status() -> tstr; muster_module answers it from a plugin-only lp_* probe (module/src/wallet/keystore_probe.nim), origin "muster_module", sync reads only (all ungated, local, no chain), at most every 5 s.
4. Settings shows the row (loadKeystoreStatus, as rln_status). A diagnostic hook MUSTER_KEYSTORE_PROBE=1 logs it.
5. scripts/keystore-self-test.sh: one offscreen runner; the logged row must carry identity {kind:module, identity:muster_module} and the default approvers. The answer to the epic's gating question, recorded in docs/labbook either way.
payload.title: K1: reach keystore_module over lp_*; caller_identity attests muster_module; read its accounts (keystore_status)

payload.description: Muster's Keystore.sign is synchronous; keystore_module has no synchronous sign. Model it like the LEZ proving pump: requestSignature(intent) -> keystore_module.request_approval({address, purpose, legs}) -> {handle, receipt}; the intents tick polls approval_status(handle, receipt); on settled/approved fetch_result -> {signed:[...]} then ack_result; cancel_approval when abandoned. The receipt is returned ONCE: memory only, never logged, never emitted. approval_settled fires only for approved/rejected, expiry (60 s unclaimed) and cancellation only show by polling. Legs: a Safe owner approval is a typed_data leg (EIP-712; the keystore computes the hash and renders every SafeTx field) and muster RE-DERIVES the safeTxHash and verifies the returned signature recovers to the chosen account before it counts (inv 1); an EIP-191 message is a message leg (printable text <= 8 KiB). Inv 2/10: the payload the keystore signs is exactly the one muster's attestation commits to. Limits: 4 live approvals per requester.
payload.title: K2: the asynchronous signing seam — request_approval → (human) → fetch_result, pumped on the intents tick

payload.description: Only QML can raise intents; muster_module returns the handle, muster_ui calls logos.request("evm.signing.approve", {handle}, cb) and settles from the module's status poll, not cb (cb is advisory: cancelled covers Back and displacement; unavailable means no signer installed, do not cancel). ui/metadata.json uses: [{"intent":"evm.signing.approve"}] as OBJECTS (a bare string array is silently ignored -> not_declared). The standalone runner has no intent shell: bundle evm_signer_ui for Basecamp, and drive self-tests headless with evm_signer_cli enrolled as an approver by the test (an operator step, never muster).
payload.title: K3: the human in the loop — muster_ui raises evm.signing.approve {handle}; headless via evm_signer_cli

payload.description: execTransaction and every other muster-originated EVM transaction go tx_sender_module.prepare -> send -> evm.signing.approve -> poll send_status until final (the poll IS the broadcast). Never sign tx legs and broadcast ourselves: that bypasses the one nonce ledger. purpose = what the room agreed; meta carries the intent id so history rows join back. Shared cap: 4 live sends across every app using tx_sender.
payload.title: K4: settlement through tx_sender_module — the device's one nonce ledger

payload.description: A member picks one of keystore_module's accounts (list_accounts + get_labels + get_account_wallets, ungated) as the secp256k1 authorization identity a room sees: account disclosure, Safe ownership checks, attestation over P (inv 10) by that account. No account yet -> hand off to evm_keystore_ui (evm.accounts.manage). FileKeystore stays the fallback when keystore_module is absent.
payload.title: K5: choose a keystore_module account as this member's Safe owner identity (disclosure + Settings)

Accepted 2026-10-01: lez/tx.nim builds LEZ v0.3.0 public transactions (shards, borsh instruction, fee declaration) held to vectors from LEZ v0.3.0's own crates (tests/vectors/lez-tx-v030, lez_tx_v030_test). On the local v0.3 zone: a FROST key owns an account and pays its own fee (2_968 vs 134_400_000 cap), a keystore member co-signs as fee payer, a wrong aggregate moves nothing (lez_frost_v030_e2e, 144 s); the room path runs end to end with lez-call v2 (lez_frost_room_v030_e2e, 75 s). lez/account_view.nim reads v0.3's sharded getAccount. Decision: FROST keeps muster's own builder (the aggregate witness is muster's); the multisig member transactions move with the program's v0.3 port (L4). Suite 187/187; runner builds.

Design note: docs/design/keystore-module-backend.md. An in-app EVM approval signs three things with one key (contribution over safeTxHash, attestation keccak256(P), F-14 binding linkDigest). The contribution maps cleanly to a typed_data leg (the keystore renders every SafeTx field; muster re-derives safeTxHash and checks recovery, inv 1). The attestation and binding are muster hash-input commitments, not EIP-712, so as they stand they would be opaque digest legs, which lets a compromised muster_module get any 32-byte hash signed in the same click. DECISION NEEDED: A (digest legs, interim, flagged) / B (typed EIP-712 attestation + binding, ADR + verifier change) / C (binding once per key at selection, K5). Recommended: C + A interim, B as target; §5 mechanics land first under either.

Correction (2026-10-01): the note above that the autopilot's full-balance shield leaves nothing for v0.3's fee is wrong. On LEZ v0.3 a privacy-preserving transaction (shield, deshield, private transfer) carries no fee field and pays none ('fee-exempt under the interim policy', lez/sequencer/core/src/fees.rs); only public transactions pay. The real issue was muster's fee estimate, a flat 1_000_000 on every rail: now 0 on the private rails and the 134_400_000 cap on a public transfer (LezAdapter.estimateFee, wallet_lez_test).

payload.description: Decided 2026-10-01 (docs/design/keystore-module-backend.md §4): until this lands, a keystore-backed approval carries muster's attestation (keccak256(P), inv 2/10) as an opaque digest leg, behind a setting and flagged on the card, because a compromised muster_module could slip any 32-byte hash into the same click. The target: a Muster EIP-712 domain with the attestation's (and the binding's) fields typed, so the keystore renders them line by line. Needs: an ADR (EIP-712 hashStruct under a domain separator is domain-separated but not muster's hash-input record, invariant 5); every member's verifier accepting the typed form beside the hash-input form (append-only probe change); a version story for old and new builds in one room. Then the digest-leg interim is removed.
payload.title: K6: typed (EIP-712) attestation and key binding for keystore-backed keys — an ADR, then verifiers that accept the typed form

payload.body: Decided (user, 2026-10-01): C + A interim, B target. Per the K2 decision (docs/design/keystore-module-backend.md §4 option C): the F-14 key binding for a keystore-backed account is requested once here, when the member selects the account (one approval, a digest leg over linkDigest for that account and context), and reused by every later approval — not re-signed per approval.

K2 pure layer landed: wallet/keystore_legs.nim (SafeTx → typed_data leg whose EIP-712 hash is checked equal to muster's safeTxHash before sending; digest legs with a stated purpose; the 64 KiB intent cap; signerOf with v 27/28 or 0/1) and wallet/keystore_requests.nim (pending table: receipts kept apart from every view, cap 4, the keystore's own states, poll cadence, deadline → cancel, fetched signatures counted only if each recovers to the chosen account over muster's own hash in leg order). payload.description: Found 2026-10-01 while porting to LEZ v0.3 (exo-eb6.4 L4). In logos-co/lez-multisig (main and PR #45, feat/lee-v0.2.4), Propose stores the caller's pda_seeds as given (multisig_program/src/propose.rs:64) and Execute passes them into the chained call unchecked (execute.rs:139). A chained call's pda_seeds authorize the callee to mutate the PDA derived from (the multisig program, seed), and every multisig's vault derives from the same program (vault seed = SHA-256('multisig_vault__' ‖ create_key)). So, as far as reading the code goes, the members of multisig A (e.g. an attacker's own 1-of-1) could propose, approve and execute a transfer naming multisig B's vault seed and move B's vault. authorized_indices likewise sets is_authorized on arbitrary target rows; whether the v0.2.4 runtime accepts that for non-PDA accounts was not checked. UNVERIFIED on a chain: confirm on infra/lez/localnet.sh with MUSTER_LEZ_VERSION=v0.2.4 (two multisigs, A drains B). The v0.3 port refuses any seed but the multisig's own vault seed at Propose and at Execute (test only_its_own_vault, red without the check). Disclosure to the lez-multisig maintainers is the operator's call; the public testnet deployment (ImageID 2ced3d30…) went with the v0.3 reset.

payload.description:
Found during L4c (exo-eb6.4.4.3). On LEZ v0.3 a public transaction whose program refuses is still INCLUDED: it reverts, keeps its fee and burns its signers' nonces (logos-execution-zone v0.3.0 lez/chain_state/src/apply.rs settle_charged_transaction: 'a failed action is ordinary execution semantics'). The sequencer RPC reports no outcome (getTransaction returns only the tx and its block; events live only in the separate indexer, and a reverted call emits none). On v0.2.4 a refused tx was dropped, so inclusion meant success.

muster's LezFrostSettlement.watch (module/src/settlement/settlement.nim, 'method watch*(s: LezFrostSettlement …) = s.adapter.finality(txRef)') returns final once LezMultisigChain.finality sees the tx included. So a FROST group's lez-call that reverts on chain (e.g. a native transfer the group's balance cannot cover after its own fee) would show FINAL in the room while nothing moved — the card would say something untrue (the educational-layer rule). LezMultisigSettlement is NOT affected: its watch waits for the proposal to read Executed. coordination/vote.nim reads a vote back, also unaffected. Check lezPump's lez-frost step too.

Fix: judge the call by the state it changes. For the native transfer the composer builds: record the recipient's (and sender's) native balance at assemble/submit and require the credit on watch; or re-derive from the block. A red-first test: lez_frost_room_v030_e2e with a transfer larger than the group's balance less its fee must NOT reach final (today it would).
payload.title: LEZ v0.3: a FROST lez-call settles 'final' on inclusion, but a refused call is included too
