payload.description:
muster_module dispatches every call synchronously on one module thread, and several chain calls had no timeout, so a hung user-configured endpoint (invariant 8: RPC is untrusted infra) blocked the whole module and every UI call behind it.

Sites: drivers/safe_rpc.nim (std/httpclient, no timeout; connect via net.dial unbounded even where a recv timeout is set — probeRpc), reached from coordinate_accounts every 10 s, coordinate_submit, connectivity; wallet/evm_rpc.nim (nim-web3 under waitFor, no budget); wallet/lez_multisig_live.nim (LezRpc under waitFor, no budget); coordinate_submit's ~4 s finality poll and legacy submit's ~10 s poll (iteration-counted, so a per-call budget multiplies by the iteration count).

Also: safeNonce read null as 0, getBalance as "", submitExecTransaction as an empty hash, LezRpc.lastBlockId as 0 and sendTransaction as "" — a failed read must raise, never read as a value.

Fix: one budget seam (wallet/rpc_budget.nim): every call is a chronos future driven under fut.wait(budget) — a total deadline over connect + headers + body — reads 5 s, sends 30 s (btc_adapter's 30 s); safe_rpc moves off std/httpclient onto it so connect is bounded too; the finality polls become wall-clock bounded and stop on the first failed read (the pump keeps watching). Tests: a local socket that accepts and never replies; every call returns an error within its budget.
payload.title: Bound every chain RPC call on the module thread; failed reads raise

payload.body: Done (uncommitted in worktree competent-swanson-341490). wallet/rpc_budget.nim: bounded(fut, budget) = waitFor fut.wait(budget), one deadline over connect+request+headers+body; reads 5 s, sends 30 s, probe 1.5 s; jsonRpc for hand-built calls. safe_rpc moved off std/httpclient (its timeout bounds recv only; net.dial connect unbounded). evm_rpc + LezRpc: every call bounded; rpcReceiptStatus now raises on a failed read (was -1). Null reads raise: safeNonce, safe getBalance, ethCall, submitExecTransaction, LezRpc lastBlockId/sendTransaction/programId. Submit finality: settlement.watchWithin (wall-clock window + one read, stops at first failed read); legacy submit 51 polls -> 4 s window. bypassesOf stops at the first failed read. Found the expensive way: making rpcReceiptStatus raise exposed a Nim 2.2.10 codegen hazard — case <raising call> with every branch assigning result skips zero-init, so EvmAdapter.finality and parts_evm.partLanded returned an unbuilt value the caller destroyed (intermittent SIGSEGV; deterministic under ASan); fixed by binding the call first, red-first verified, written up in the labbook. Tests: tests/rpc_budget_test.nim (silent socket that accepts and never replies, 28 calls within budget, worst overrun 3 ms; a null-answering endpoint), ASan-clean 8/8. run-suite.sh 211/211 green; anvil e2e green: coordinate_submit_anvil, safe_anvil_e2e, safe_real_anvil_e2e, split_anvil_e2e, split_erc20_anvil_e2e, settle_up_erc20_anvil_e2e, settle_up_across_anvil_e2e. Follow-ups offered as chips: btc_adapter connect under the budget; per-endpoint cooldown after a timeout.

payload.description:
BitcoindAdapter.call (wallet/btc_adapter.nim) uses std/httpclient with timeout = 30_000. That bounds each recv only; the connect (net.dial) has no timeout, so a user-configured Bitcoin node address that drops SYNs hangs the single module dispatch thread for the kernel TCP timeout (~2 min). Invariant 8: the node is untrusted, user-configured infrastructure. exo-14f moved every other chain call onto wallet/rpc_budget.nim and left this one as a follow-up.

Fix: the call becomes a chronos HTTP request (HttpSessionRef / HttpClientRequestRef) under bounded(fut, budget) — one deadline over connect, request, headers and body. Reads readBudget() (5 s), sendrawtransaction sendBudget() (30 s), scantxoutset its own explicit budget (a mainnet UTXO-set scan legitimately takes minutes). Not nim-json-rpc's RpcHttpClient: it raises on a non-2xx status before reading the body, and bitcoind answers an RPC error with HTTP 500 and the error JSON in the body — today's messages ("bitcoind sendrawtransaction: min relay fee not met (-26)") must survive. Basic auth from the URL userinfo, /wallet/<name> routing, redactUserinfo kept: no credentials in a message.

Tests: rpc_budget_test gains a silent-endpoint case per btc call (an error within its budget) and an HTTP 500 endpoint with a bitcoind error body (the node's message, not the status).
payload.title: btc_adapter: the Bitcoin node's calls under the RPC budget (connect bounded)

payload.body: Done 2026-10-05, PR corpetty/muster#224 (stacked on #223, exo-14f). BitcoindAdapter.call now drives chronos HttpSessionRef/HttpClientRequestRef under bounded(fut, budget), reading the body whatever the status (bitcoind's HTTP 500/404 carry the error object; nim-json-rpc's client would raise on the status first). Budgets: reads readBudget 5 s, sendrawtransaction sendBudget 30 s, probeBitcoind probeBudget 1.5 s (as probeRpc), scantxoutset new ScanBudget 5 min (a judgment: one pass over >10^8 mainnet coins; Core gives it a status action). Connect within a read's budget on every call (chronos connectTimeout), headers timer set past the budget (chronos's 120 s default would end a long scan). No scantxoutset abort (node-global). A failure status with no error object now raises. Tests: rpc_budget_test §6 (every btc call within budget on a silent endpoint; a SYN-dropping address — full accept queue — within a read's budget, scan and broadcast included) and §7 (Core-like HTTP 500/404 bodies as the node's message, 401 named, no credentials in any message, /wallet/<name> routing); red-first vs the old adapter (getblockcount waited 30 s on readLine). Hand-checked against Bitcoin Core 31.1 regtest. run-suite.sh on Nim 2.2.12: 209/211; the 2 failures reproduce at the base and are environmental: probe_audit_settlement_stepper (2.2.12 refuses a lent capture; 2.2.10 pinned) and probe_return_marshalling_host (host glibc 2.39 vs nixpkgs libsodium's 2.44, harness load). e2e each on a fresh regtest: btc_regtest_e2e, split_btc_regtest_e2e, phase_d_exit_test, settle_up_btc_regtest_e2e all PASS. The e2e tests' own node admin passes 120 s (mining 101 blocks into a wallet took 7.3 s under load).

No-funds part ran on the live testnet (2026-10-02): split-lez-testnet.sh with MUSTER_FLEET=local — two real lez_core 0.5.0 wallets scanned block 0 → tip 3141 and followed the tip (~33 s blocks; v0.3's 256-bit private ids hold for the scan), A proposed the private split, B named its account (e043cb2a…75b6, reused on relaunch), and the run stops naming the funder to fund. Blocked on funding: the testnet funder Public/5fwr3Z2u73ZoXmasgac2pqot29fmn9AxvWQu4uQQUXGq holds 0. Suggested ask: ~1 LEZ (10^9 base units) covers a full L5 pass with room: the multisig deploy 3.46M, 3 members × 50M, FROST group 200M, the split 1000 + fees.

payload.description:
Design: docs/design/side-modules.md (survey at e75ec71, 2026-10-02).

muster_module runs in one process: keys, the room kernel (epoch crypto, log, authentication, folds, drivers, the invariant 1/2/10 gates, assemble) and every outside-world call (chain reads, broadcast, finality watching, part confirmation). The rule this epic implements: what touches the outside world may leave the process; what touches room plaintext or keys stays (keys leave only to a platform key holder, exo-149). Folds do NOT move out — they need decrypted room data, the event plane carries no auth token, and a Nim provider cannot see its caller.

Four structural problems block any offload and come first: the module has no clock (every pump runs inside coordinate_intents, active room only); one implicit active room (gSession, read by driverFor); a pull-only whole-state UI contract (~7.7 calls/s, each re-reducing the full log, no events); domain rules in QML.

Plan S1–S8 (children): room context explicit → kernel tick → events → fold cache; domain rules out of QML; sign split from broadcast; EVM onto the official evm-wallet modules; a key-less chain watcher module.
payload.title: Side-modules: a kernel that keeps the log, keys and gates; outside IO moves to other modules

payload.description:
Design: docs/design/side-modules.md §3, §7 (epic exo-ff5).

Today every room method acts on the global active room gSession/gTopic (module/nim-lib/muster_module.nim:632-634), set by coordinate_join. driverFor → driverForKind → driverForPolicy(kind, roomAccounts(), roomDriver, …) (muster_module.nim:191-202) reads roomAccounts() = reduceAccounts(gSession.roomEvents()) (:654-659) and room-kind drivers read the roster from gSession.members() — inputs the fold was never given. coordinate_conversations swaps gSession per room just to make driverFor resolve (:3566-3575).

Do: introduce a RoomCtx {session, accounts, roster} passed explicitly; DriverFor becomes (kind, RoomCtx) -> Driver; folds and pumps take the ctx; room-scoped lidl methods take a topic (keep the topic-less forms as thin wrappers over the active room for the UI until it migrates). The conversations swap disappears. Acceptance: a test folds two rooms with different disclosed accounts in one process without touching a global, and conversations returns the same as today. Prerequisite for S2 (tick across rooms) and S4 (a cache key that captures every input).
payload.title: S1 Room context explicit: topic-scoped room methods, driverFor takes the room

payload.description:
Design: docs/design/side-modules.md §3, §7 (epic exo-ff5).

Every pump runs inside coordinate_intents and only for the active room (module/nim-lib/muster_module.nim:2117-2122: gSession.poll, lezPump, frostPump, splitPump, keystorePump). The UI's 1 s Room timer (ui/src/qml/Room.qml ~3001) is therefore the module's heartbeat: a split payment in a room that is not open is neither reported nor confirmed (splitPump acts on gSession only, :1174ff), and headless logoscore advances nothing. Reads also trigger network (gSession.poll fires store queries).

Do: one coordinate_tick() that, for EVERY joined session, drains transport + runs the pumps under that room's RoomCtx (S1); coordinate_intents/messages/members/activity/… become pure reads of current state. Callers: the UI timer calls tick (once, not six reads), and headless runs can call it too. Rate-limits stay per pump. Open question recorded in the doc: can a Nim core module own a timer that safely schedules work on its own module thread (it has no event loop today)?

Acceptance: a two-room test where a split part lands in the room that is NOT active, and one tick reports + confirms it. Depends on S1.
payload.title: S2 Kernel clock: coordinate_tick advances every joined room; reads become side-effect free

payload.description:
Design: docs/design/side-modules.md §3, §4, §7 (epic exo-ff5).

muster.lidl declares no events and muster_module never emits, though the SDK has emit() (logos_sdk/api) and muster_gen.nim installs the emit callback. The UI polls ~7.7 calls/s with a room open (Room.qml 1 s / 5 s / 10 s timers, Main.qml 2 s timers), each returning whole room state, and the C++ backend re-parses whole blobs into JS arrays (ListView models reset).

Do: declare events in muster.lidl — e.g. room_changed(topic, head), intent_changed(topic, intent_id, state), pending_changed(topic), conversations_changed() — carrying ids and log heads ONLY: the event plane carries no auth token, so no plaintext, no effect JSON, no names. Emit from S2's tick on the module thread (the SDK's gEmit is a threadvar; a foreign-thread emit is a silent no-op). The UI subscribes (C++ onEvent / QML logos.onModuleEvent) and re-reads only what changed; keep a slow poll backstop (events are lost across a provider restart — atlas guides/calling-official-modules.md §4). Related: exo-607.11 (typed list models, signals with args). Depends on S2.
payload.title: S3 Push: plaintext-free events from muster_module; the UI subscribes, polls only as a backstop

payload.description:
Design: docs/design/side-modules.md §3 (epic exo-ff5).

No fold is cached: every read re-reduces the whole log (roomEvents copies the log and recomputes event ids, authorship.nim:184-196). canonicalOrder (module/src/log/log.nim:50-86) re-sorts the ready set each step and deletes its head — roughly quadratic — and recomputes eventId (dCBOR + SHA-256) per event per call; it runs in reduceIntents, reduceIntentViews, intentContext, intentInputs, intentRecord, reduceAccounts, intentProvenance, reduceActivity, logProvenance — several times per intent per call. Each driverOf call re-does roomEvents + reduceAccounts (intents.nim:149 and passes). coordinate_intents runs every second.

Do: memoize canonical order + the per-room fold set keyed by (log head set, roster epoch, disclosed accounts) — every input S1 made explicit — and invalidate on ingest. Make canonicalOrder a heap-based topo sort with cached ids. Invariant 4 unaffected: the cache is a pure function of its key. Acceptance: a property test that cached and uncached folds agree under reorder/duplication (extend probe_live_convergence-style tests; tests are append-only), plus a measured per-tick cost on a 1k-event room. Depends on S1.
payload.title: S4 Fold cache keyed by log head; canonicalOrder in O(N log N)

payload.description:
Design: docs/design/side-modules.md §3 (epic exo-ff5).

Rules that decide what is proposed or agreed live only in the UI, so every UI (the seaqt port, exo-607.8, included) must copy them:
- Room.qml:621-637 proposeFrom builds the Safe effect in QML; value via parseInt (a JSON Number: exact only to 2^53 wei), nonce from coordinate_account with a silent fallback to 0. Statement/invoke/add-driver effects also built in QML (Room.qml ~905-950, ~1780) while split/BTC/LEZ/settle-up effects are built by the module from parameters.
- Room.qml:776-880 split preview math (ethToWei, divSmall, fiatTotal, splitPreview) re-implements drivers/split.nim evenShares/fiatQuote; Room.qml:844 fiat decimals table, :351 BTC dust 546 copied.
- Room.qml:405-412 the propose gate (members >= threshold, else 2) exists only in QML.
- Room.qml:574/596 auto-admit + re-ask decisions, state held only in the UI.
- Composer.qml:127-134 room topic from Math.random (not a CSPRNG) — the unguessable-topic property of exo-661.7 belongs in the module.
- Main.qml:167 contentTopicOf copies toContentTopic; RoomAccounts.qml:36-41 copies the CAIP-2 Bitcoin table; MusterCard.qml ready/partState/myTransfer re-judge what the module's views already say.

Do: module methods that build every effect from typed parameters (decimal strings, never JS Number), a preview method for splits, the propose gate + topic minting (CSPRNG) + admission policy in the module; the UI renders. Related: exo-607.8 (less backend logic to port).
payload.title: S5 Domain rules out of QML into the module

payload.description:
Design: docs/design/side-modules.md §5, §7 (epic exo-ff5).

The outside-world seams fuse the key step with the IO step, so IO cannot leave the process without taking the key with it: ChainAdapter.submit(tx, ks) signs EIP-155 inside evm_adapter.nim (~137); EvmPartSeam pays via adapter.submit (parts_evm.nim ~52); BtcPartSeam signs DER inside the seam (parts_btc.nim ~43); LezMultisigLive takes a witness closure (multisig_chain.nim ~165) and signs with lezMemberSign; keystore bindingFor / signLegacyTransfer pass closures over ks.sign.

Do: kernel-side sign(prepared, ks) -> raw bytes, seam-side broadcast(raw) / observe(ref); reads return {value, source, height} so the kernel records the read event (invariant 10, attest.nim readEvent) and does every comparison (invariants 1, 8). No behaviour change; every existing e2e (safe_anvil_e2e, split_anvil_e2e, split_btc_regtest_e2e, lez_multisig_live_e2e, …) stays green. Prerequisite for S7 and S8.
payload.title: S6 Separate signing from broadcasting at the chain seams; reads return value + source

payload.description:
Design: docs/design/side-modules.md §5 (epic exo-ff5).

Basecamp 0.3.1's catalog ships the EVM stack muster re-implements in-process: eth_rpc_module (per-chain, fail-closed JSON-RPC, optional verified routing via verified_proxy_module), fee_module, tx_sender_module (the device's one nonce ledger; calls approved as one human decision in keystore_module). Atlas: stacks/evm-wallet.md, stacks/key-custody.md 'Recipes for a third-party module (Muster)'.

exo-149.4 moves Safe settlement (execTransaction) to tx_sender_module. This task covers the rest: EVM reads (balances, Safe owners/threshold/nonce, receipts for part confirmation, token info) through eth_rpc_module; split-part payments (EvmPartSeam) and wallet_send through tx_sender_module; fee estimates through fee_module. The in-process path (evm_rpc / evm_sign / safe_rpc) stays as the standalone-runner fallback, where keystore_module cannot attest muster (keystore-module-backend.md §1). Invariant 8: muster's Settings still show which endpoint each read used (eth_rpc_module replies carry a route). Depends on S6 and exo-149.4.
payload.title: S7 EVM onto the official evm-wallet modules: eth_rpc_module reads, tx_sender_module sends

payload.description:
Design: docs/design/side-modules.md §6 (epic exo-ff5).

A new logos core module that holds no key and sees no room plaintext. In: watch({ref, chain, kind: tx|output|inclusion|nonce, target, endpoint}), unwatch(ref), broadcast(chain, raw, endpoint) — every tx already signed by the kernel (S6), every endpoint passed from muster's settings (invariant 8). Out: an observed(ref, seq) event (ids only — no auth on the event plane) + observations(since) for the values {value, source, height}. muster's kernel records each as a read event (invariant 10) and does every comparison (invariants 1, 8); the watcher's only state is its watch list, which the kernel re-sends on restart (invariant 4: the log + pending book stay the truth). It owns a real timer, so finality and part confirmation progress without the UI and across rooms.

Moves out: the IO halves of splitPump (BTC/EVM part landed/gone, the creditor's confirmation reads), lezPump (LEZ multisig inclusion), coordinate_submit's ~4 s in-call finality wait (muster_module.nim ~2991), BitcoindAdapter reads/broadcast. Stays: frostPump (no IO), keystorePump (key path), Settlement.assemble, checkRead, every read record. No official Bitcoin module exists (atlas gaps.md) — decide whether this generalizes into one. Watch the out-of-process token handshake trap (docs/labbook/logoscore-out-of-process-module-auth.md). Depends on S2, S6.
payload.title: S8 A key-less chain watcher module: broadcast + observe for Bitcoin, LEZ multisig, Safe finality, part confirmation

payload.description: Found bringing up the new machine (2026-10-02, Ubuntu 24.04, glibc 2.39). run-suite.sh borrows libsodium from the floating registry nixpkgs (nixpkgs-unstable, now glibc 2.44) but compiles and links with the host's gcc, so every test binary loads the host's libc.so.6 and dies at run time: "GLIBC_ABI_GNU2_TLS not found (required by …libsodium.so.26)". First full run: 70 pass, 280 fail, every failure that one line. The old machine passed only because its registry snapshot was older. Fix: take libsodium and gcc from ONE nix build (one nixpkgs resolution) and put that gcc on PATH whenever the suite borrows nixpkgs' libsodium; MUSTER_SODIUM keeps the host compiler. Not fixed here: scripts/grade-specs.sh has the same mix (host gcc from the oracle's allowlisted PATH, a /nix/store-walk libsodium in probe_return_marshalling_host) — unverifiable on this host until nim is reachable from /usr/local/bin (the oracle's PATH is .venv/bin + a fixed tool list + /usr/local/bin:/usr/bin:/bin; choosenim's nim is under ~/.choosenim).
payload.title: run-suite.sh links nixpkgs' libsodium with the host's gcc: every test fails on a host glibc older than nixpkgs'

payload.description: Seen 2026-10-02 on the new machine: scripts/grade-specs.sh exo-a90.17 → FileNotFoundError: 'nim'. exophial's oracle runs probes on PATH = graded .venv/bin + a fixed tool symlink dir (uv git bash sh pb check-jsonschema pre-commit claude) + /usr/local/bin:/usr/bin:/bin, and this host's nim is choosenim's (~/.nimble/bin shim → ~/.choosenim/toolchains/nim-2.2.2/bin/nim; the shim needs the real HOME, which the oracle replaces). Host remedy (root): ln -s ~/.choosenim/toolchains/nim-2.2.2/bin/nim /usr/local/bin/nim — the real binary, not the shim. Then expect exo-844's glibc failure here too: the probes compile with the allowlisted PATH's host gcc against .probe-env/sodium (nixpkgs), and probe_return_marshalling_host links its harness with host g++ against whichever libsodium a /nix/store walk finds first. Likely fix: grade-specs.sh links nixpkgs' gcc wrapper into .probe-env beside sodium (one nix build), tests/probes/config.nims sets gcc.exe/gcc.linkerexe from it, and the marshalling probe prefers .probe-env/{g++,sodium} when MUSTER_NIMPKGS is unset (the grader's signal, as closurePaths already uses). Related: exo-844, exo-aa7 (upstream asks for exophial).

payload.description: Found in the two-machine split run (exo-a90.21, 2026-10-02). Alice (server) founded muster.room.6ac8ea9cdc366149 with Bob (workstation), proposed a split, and was killed mid-collection (R-4/R-6). Relaunched without --fresh (identity, contacts and data kept), her Home read 'Nothing on yet' and the Room tab offered only 'Join a room' with an empty topic field. The module never re-enters a room on start: musterCoordinateConversations lists gSessions, which hold only rooms joined since launch, and nothing persists the joined set (contacts, dismissed invites and the keystore persist; rooms do not). The founder has no invite to fall back on, and a joiner's invite is cleared for good once joined. Typing the topic into 'Join a room' worked: the room caught up from the store, every event since the kill included (Bob's agreement and payment), and Alice's client confirmed his part from its own chain read, so the room went final. docs/runbooks/client-tour.md:661 says the opposite ('after a restart its row is titled by its topic'). Expected: on start, the module re-joins every room this member joined (persisted beside the keystore, as contacts are), so Home lists them; state = reduce(log) already makes the rest work.
payload.title: A relaunched member's rooms are gone: Home is empty, and the only way back is typing the topic

payload.description: intentIdFor(effect, policy) = keccak(effect ++ '|' ++ policy)[:8] content-addresses an intent, but only the audit verifier (audit.nim:409) re-checks it. Any admitted member can publish a second intent/<id>/propose (or /policy) with a different effect under an existing id. effectJsonOf / intentPolicyOf return the first match in ARRIVAL order, and planApproval (live.nim:126) signs canonicalize(driverFor(intentPolicyOf), effectJsonOf); reduceIntents pass 1 takes the first propose in CANONICAL order (ties by smallest event id: grindable). So members can fold different effects for one id, and the card can differ from what a member signs: invariants 1 and 4. Fix: a propose/policy pair counts only if intentIdFor(effect, policy) == id, in ONE place every reader of intent/<id>/propose|policy uses (effectJsonOf, intentPolicyOf, reduceIntents, intentInputs, approvalParents, activity, provenance, room_infra); effectJsonOf/intentPolicyOf in canonical order. Red-first test: a substitute delivered in both orders, every member folds the honest effect.
payload.title: A substitute intent/<id>/propose|policy under an honest intent's id is folded: the fold path never checks the id is content-addressed

payload.body: Fix on fix/rooms-survive-relaunch (stacked on fix/k5-rep-slot): coordination/joined_rooms.nim persists the joined set (joined_rooms.json beside the keystore, in join order); coordinate_join remembers each room; coordinate_start_inbox (the UI's startup call, C++ at context-ready, retried) re-enters every remembered room once per run, none made active, returning {inbox, rooms}. Not in scope: the intents-tick pumps (split confirm/pay, LEZ, FROST, keystore) still run only for the ACTIVE room, so a restored room that is never opened does not pump — true of any non-active room today.

Verified 2026-10-02. scripts/relaunch-self-test.sh (MUSTER_FLEET=local): red on the runner built before the fix ('remembered: none', nothing re-entered); green on this branch's runner ('rooms restored=1' for the joined topic ~3 s after the relaunch, no join). On a display, the run's own Alice (Xvfb, live logos.dev fleet, the server's anvil): on this build she joined muster.room.6ac8ea9cdc366149 once (joined_rooms.json written), was killed and relaunched without --fresh, and with nothing typed Home listed 'Done · /muster/1/muster.room.6ac8ea9cdc366149/proto · 1 settled'; opening it from Home showed the settled split, 2 in the room, the full history and the flow view (23 actions). Suite on the branch: 211/211.

Correction to the description: the split was already final before Alice was killed. Her log: 20:40:20 proposed (collecting 1/2), 20:40:28 Bob agreed (executable 2/2), Bob's payment in anvil block 10 at 20:40:34, 20:40:35 her client confirmed it (final); the kill came at 20:40:38. So the manual rejoin rebuilt a FINISHED room from the store (every event, the confirmation included); it did not catch up on events made while she was down. The bug stands as described; the R-4/R-6 kill-mid-collection check is still to do (exo-a90.21).

2026-10-02, the EVM half end to end across two machines: Alice on the compute server (bugger, Xvfb, try-peer.sh), Bob on the user's workstation (try-peer.sh, the server's anvil + bitcoind through an ssh tunnel), both on the live logos.dev fleet, both runners built from main + #215 + #217. Alice opened a room with Bob from 'Start something → Split a bill' (invite → join → admitted, epoch 1), proposed 0.01 ETH ('dinner, two machines'; Bob owes 0.005); 20:40:20 proposed, 20:40:28 Bob agreed, 20:40:34 Bob paid from his own key (tx 0x900163a688a67cbcde9c4313d2bc9b1e58ebdd3f89ce9db89fe55d1a0367eeaf, block 10, exactly 5000000000000000 wei Bob→Alice), 20:40:35 Alice's client confirmed it from its own RPC read → final on both. NOT yet done: the R-4/R-6 kill mid-collection — the kill landed 3 s after final. Its relaunch found exo-ecbe (rooms lost on relaunch; fixed in #219). Still open here: the R-4/R-6 rerun (kill before the debtor agrees) and the private split across the two machines.

Fix: proposalOf(events, id) in intent_events.nim returns the (effect, policy) pair the id is the content address of — a propose/policy counts only if intentIdFor(effect, policy) == id (policy '' = a legacy policy-less propose), and the effect must parse as JSON (else effect++'|'++policy is not injective: the honest effect and policy joined by '|', proposed with no policy, hash to the same id — mutation-checked in the test). Choice is a pure function of the event set (canonical order only when two pairs are valid, i.e. a keccak collision on the 8-byte id). Every reader goes through it: effectJsonOf, intentPolicyOf, reduceIntents pass 1 (+ per-fold memo), reduceIntentViews, reduceActivity, intentProvenance, logProvenance, intentInputs (P), approvalParents, room_infra.proposedIntents, liveReannounce. Red-first test: module/tests/intent_id_binding_test.nim (Room3: Carol's substitutes ground to sort first, before/after Alice's propose, safe+threshold; 7 delivery orders; audit verifies; orphan ids fold to nothing). Tests moved to content-addressed ids (their negatives would have passed vacuously): multiparty_intent, threshold_fold, frost_room, governance, kinds; probe_split_convergence_stepper now uses the policy-less id (its 8 events carry no policy decl). Probe time 169s vs 162s on main after taking canonicalOrder/parseJson off the common path. Follow-up spawned: intent/<id>/context has the same substitution gap.

payload.description: Found writing exo-ecbe (#219). The intents-tick pumps — splitPump (report my landed payments, confirm what paid me), lezPump, frostPump, keystorePump — run from musterCoordinateIntents, which serves only gSession, the ACTIVE room, and is polled by the Room view's tick. So a room the member is not looking at does none of it: a creditor whose debtor paid while their Room tab shows another room (or Home) never confirms the part, and the split never goes final, until they open that room. True of any non-active room today; exo-ecbe's restored rooms inherit it (re-entered at startup, none made active). Expected: every joined room pumps, whichever is open — e.g. musterCoordinateConversations (Home's 1 s poll over every session) or a module-side tick runs each session's pumps under that session, as conversations already swaps gSession per room for homeItems. Watch: the pumps assume gSession/gTopic globals (splitPump passes gTopic, gSession to pumpBook; seamOfPending(gSession, …)), so each must run with its room swapped in, and the LEZ/keystore pumps' rate limits are global. Related: exo-ecbe, exo-a90.23 (payments in flight).
payload.title: A room's confirmations and payments pump only while it is the open room

payload.description: Seen 2026-10-02 in the two-machine run (exo-a90.21). Room muster.room.6ac8ea9cdc366149 held, in time order: Bob admitted (epoch 1), split 1 (proposed 20:40:20, agreed, paid, confirmed), then split 2 'R-4/R-6 rerun' (proposed 21:54:58 … confirmed 22:07:52). Alice's Room history listed split 2's whole group FIRST — proposed, approved ×2, ready, settled, confirmed — then the admit, then split 1. reduceActivity (coordination/intents.nim) groups each intent's lines by the canonical index of its propose event, and canonicalOrder among parentless events is smallest-content-id-first, so groups land in hash order; the code comment names it ('interleaved multi-intent timing without an authored clock is a known limit'). Single-intent rooms read right; any room with two proposals reads out of order, and the admit can sit between unrelated groups. The panel also auto-scrolls to its end, so the misplaced group was off-screen above and the first thing in view was split 2's settle/confirm lines. Possible fix without a wall clock: order groups by causal position — an intent proposed after another intent's events reached its proposer can cite them (a parent link), or by each group's first event's position in the proposer's arrival order — anything deterministic over the event set (invariant 4) that respects happens-before.
payload.title: Room history orders proposals by content hash: a later proposal is listed above the room's earlier history

payload.body: R-4/R-6 rerun PASSED (2026-10-02), the EVM split across the two machines. Alice (server, #219 build) proposed 'R-4/R-6 rerun', 0.004 ETH with Bob owing 0.002: published collecting 1/2 at 21:54:58, and Alice was killed at 21:55:01, before Bob saw it. Bob (workstation; his runner also restarted, rejoined by topic) agreed and paid while Alice was down: anvil block 11 at 22:06:26, Bob→Alice exactly 2000000000000000 wei (tx 0x25ff105bc87aa38e61734541594c48d141c7f0b6a9ffd1e2fa24a805f9d0d87e). Alice relaunched at 22:06:59 without --fresh: Home listed the room by itself ('rooms restored=1', 'Waiting on others · 1 in progress'); nothing confirmed while the room was closed (exo-273); opened from Home at 22:07:52, her client read Bob's payment from her own RPC and the split went final the same second (agreed 2/2, confirmed 1/1). Found: the room history's out-of-order groups (filed). Still open here: the private split across the two machines.

payload.description: Found fixing exo-dbd (substitute propose/policy under an intent id). intentContext(events, id) in module/src/coordination/attest.nim returns the FIRST intent/<id>/context in canonical order, with no check of who published it or that it belongs to the proposal; canonical ties break by smallest event id, which any epoch-key holder can grind (e.g. junk parents, ignored when absent). The context is not covered by the id hash (keccak(effect|policy)[:8]). Consequences (by reading, no test yet): (1) attestationPayload P is built from it, so a member publishing a substitute context ground to sort first changes P for every member who receives it; approvals already attested over the honest P are then REJECTED by reduceIntents' attestation gate (pass 2, 'if not ok: continue') — one member can void every approval of any intent after the fact, or choose the expiry/account approvals bind to (invariant 2); (2) planApproval / liveSubmitPrecheck / liveProposeIntent's expired-duplicate check (live.nim) read it, so a substitute with a past expiry makes an honest intent look expired. Fix options: the proposer signs the context (the proposer claim intent/<id>/proposer/<who> is already author-signed, authorship.nim), or the context is committed in the propose/id, or a second context refuses rather than picks — mind liveReannounce (re-publishes the context into a new epoch) and the audit file (carries it). Red-first test: follow module/tests/intent_id_binding_test.nim (Room3: Carol substitutes a context under Alice's intent, ground to sort first, before and after approvals; approvals over the honest context still count and every member folds the honest context). Then module/tests/run-suite.sh whole suite green.
payload.title: A substitute intent/<id>/context is folded: intentContext takes the first in canonical order, bound to nothing

payload.description: module/tests/probes/probe_audit_settlement_stepper.nim:25 fails on Nim 2.2.12 (nixpkgs' current nim): "'policy' is of type <lent string> which cannot be captured as it would violate memory safety". In stageCorrect, 'for policy in LivePolicies:' yields a lent string and the nested 'proc approve(who)' captures it. The pinned Nim 2.2.10 accepts it. Fix: copy the loop variable before the closure ('let policy = policy'); the probe's checks do not change. Also sweep the other probes/tests for the same pattern (a for-loop variable over a seq/array captured by a nested proc) and run the whole suite on 2.2.12. The probe is derived-exo-403 s6's oracle, so scripts/grade-specs.sh exo-403 must stay green. Found 2026-10-05 running the full suite for exo-496 (corpetty/muster#224); reproduces at fix/rpc-budget (corpetty/muster#223), independent of both.
payload.title: probe_audit_settlement_stepper fails to compile on Nim 2.2.12 (lent loop var captured by closure)

payload.body: Root cause upstream: nim-lang/Nim#25860 (fixes #25849, #25872; in v2.2.12 and devel) made items over an ARRAY yield lent T, as seqs/openArrays already did; LivePolicies is a const array, so the loop variable became lent and the long-standing no-capture-of-lent rule applied. Fixed with 'let policy = policy'. Verified: full suite on 2.2.12 212/212 (this probe was the only failure in the repo); the probe passes on 2.2.10; grade-specs.sh exo-403 8/8 (the grader is hermetic and always compiles with /usr/local/bin/nim = 2.2.10 here, so the probe was also run in the grader's invocation form with 2.2.12: red without the fix, green with it). The audit-download check ran against main's Oct 2 runner (this change touches no runner input); a fresh make build OOMed this host in flake evaluation (nix evaluator >7 GB), not in compilation.

payload.description:
Follow-up to exo-14f (PR #223). Every chain call on the module thread now has a budget, but the budgets stack across calls: coordinate_accounts every 10 s runs chainViewOf + bypassesOf per disclosed account (each a probeRpc then 1-2 reads), connectivity probes every 5 s, and the pumps on the intents tick read receipts every 2 s. A node that answers eth_chainId but hangs eth_call, or several disclosed Safe accounts on a silent node, keeps the module busy most of every window (two Safe accounts on a hung node: ~20 s in one coordinate_accounts call, the UI call's own timeout).

Fix: a per-endpoint cooldown in wallet/rpc_budget.nim. After an endpoint (keyed by its URL, never written into a message) gives no answer within a budget, a read or probe to it fails at once with RpcTimeoutError (a RpcCoolingError) that names the call that went unanswered, when, and when the endpoint is tried again. The first call after the cooldown is sent; any answer clears it. A broadcast is always sent (it is the user's own action), and its timeout starts a cooldown for reads. The failure stays an error, never a value. The UI-visible details (connectivity row, account check 'unknown', readiness) say 'not asked' with the times instead of 'unreachable'.

Tests: rpc_budget_test — a second call inside the cooldown returns in ~0 ms, a call after it is sent, a recovered endpoint is used again, a send is not held, another endpoint is not affected, the message carries no URL.
payload.title: Per-endpoint cooldown after an RPC timeout, so budgets do not stack on the module thread

payload.body: Done (PR #225, stacked on #223; commit 8db633e). wallet/rpc_budget.nim: after a no-answer within a budget an endpoint (keyed by URL, never in a message) cools down: a read or probe raises RpcCoolingError (an RpcTimeoutError) at once, naming the unanswered call, when, and the next try; the first call after the cooldown is sent; any successful answer ends it. 15 s, doubled per no-answer in a row, up to 60 s. Sends are always sent; their no-answer starts a cooldown for reads. onEndpoint wraps jsonRpc (Safe), evm_rpc's rpcTry (connect timeout now counts) and the LEZ client's call. Status lines say 'RPC not asked: it did not answer …; next try at …' (probeRpc + Safe owner/module/guard/threshold reads), shown as is by the connectivity row, an account's unknown check and readiness. Settings re-naming rpc / lez-rpc ends its cooldown. The LEZ client no longer writes the sequencer URL into errors. Labbook section added. Tests: rpc_budget_test §6 against an endpoint that holds then answers (refusal 0 ms through every seam, no URL, send still sent, other endpoint unaffected, doubling to the cap, first call after sent, recovered endpoint used again and count reset, forgetCooldown, zero = off); red with the refusal disabled (401 ms). run-suite.sh: 209/211 under nixpkgs Nim 2.2.12 + host g++; the 2 others pass in the project's toolchain: probe_audit_settlement_stepper on Nim 2.2.10 (2.2.12 refuses its lent capture; fails identically on the base 0d11ba6), probe_return_marshalling_host with nixpkgs gcc (host g++ + nixpkgs libsodium = glibc mismatch). anvil e2e not run here. Follow-up offered: keep the EVM RPC URL out of rpcChainCaip2's detail and the connectivity row / MUSTER-LP log.

payload.description:
The hosted module copied the user's configured endpoint URLs whole into text that leaves it, and a hosted RPC URL often carries credentials: a key in the path (https://mainnet.infura.io/v3/<key>), in the query, or userinfo (http://user:pass@host). Invariant 8: RPC is user-configured, untrusted infrastructure; its credentials are not copied into messages or logs.

Sites (module/nim-lib/muster_module.nim unless named): rpcChainCaip2() put gRpcUrl into "your RPC (...) did not answer" (the Split composer; logged under gLpDebug); musterConnectivity() put "endpoint": gRpcUrl into the RPC row, and the whole result goes to stderr as "MUSTER-LP connectivity" (ConnectionIndicators.qml shows it before the detail); coordination/readiness.nim's infra details "rpc = <url>" and "lez-rpc = <url>" (the card; the MUSTER-LP readiness log); the settings reply (rpc, lez.rpc whole; btcRpc through redactUserinfo, which masks the password only, never a key in the path); coordinate_submit's Bitcoin error (redactUserinfo).

Fix: wallet/redact.nim redactUrl(url) = scheme://host[:port], "***@" for any userinfo, "/***" for any path, query or fragment, "***" whole when it does not parse with a plain host and numeric port, "" for none. Used at every site above. rpcChainCaip2(url) moves to coordination/parts_evm.nim and the RPC row to readiness.rpcConnectivityRow, so a test can drive both. The connectivity row shows the redacted endpoint (it still names the host being probed); Settings shows the redacted form too (it only displays the value, never reads it back; settings.json keeps the URL whole). Test: tests/rpc_url_redaction_test.nim.

Not here: the LEZ client's errors (wallet/lez_multisig_live.nim, "LEZ <meth> at <url>" and three more on fix/rpc-budget) reach the room's "the LEZ sequencer: ..." and "sequencer-unreachable" details; exo-14f.1 (claude/sleepy-ride-imq68m) drops the URL from them, so this branch leaves that file alone. btc_adapter's redactUserinfo is deprecated, not removed: exo-496's rpc_budget_test (claude/great-ritchie-2st4nl) still names it.
payload.title: Configured RPC URLs reach the UI and the MUSTER-LP log whole; a hosted endpoint's key leaks

payload.body: Done (2026-10-05) on claude/gifted-gates-mkc30c (fix/rpc-budget + main, since exo-14f is not on main yet): 917ddbf. wallet/redact.nim redactUrl; the split composer's RPC error (parts_evm.rpcChainCaip2), the RPC connectivity row (readiness.rpcConnectivityRow, which musterConnectivity logs), the readiness details, coordinate_submit's Bitcoin error and the settings reply all show an endpoint redacted. tests/rpc_url_redaction_test.nim, red with any one site reverted to the raw URL. run-suite.sh 213/214 with Nim 2.2.12 (nixpkgs); the one failure, probe_audit_settlement_stepper, also failed on the commit before this change (a closure captured a lent loop variable, refused by 2.2.12) and is fixed in the next commit; it passes alone. Revised (2026-10-05, per the user): what stays on this user's own screen may show a secret; what must never carry one is the room. Checked: no room event carries a configured URL (external reads cite fixed labels such as bitcoind:scantxoutset, lez:getAccount, lez:testnet@<height>; part reports carry a tx ref). So the settings reply carries each endpoint whole again, beside its redactUrl form (rpcMasked, btcRpcMasked, lez.rpcMasked), and Settings.qml shows the masked form with a Show/Hide per field (view state only). Text that is logged or quoted stays redacted: the split composer's RPC error, the readiness details, the connectivity row and its MUSTER-LP line (these get copied into labbook entries and issues; the host stays visible).

Settings Show/Hide (7018b62), how it was checked: the runner did not build in this session (its flake inputs need ~34 GitHub repos this session cannot fetch), so not on a display. Instead the real ui/src/qml/Settings.qml was loaded headless (qml from nixpkgs Qt 6.11.2, offscreen) inside a harness with stand-in Logos.Theme / Logos.Controls (Text, Button, TextField) and a fake backend: no QML warning on load; 9/9 checks pass (masked first; Show only where something is hidden; whole after Show; Hide masks again). qmllint: no new warning kinds. payload.body: Root cause found and fixed on fix/rpc-test-segv (2026-10-06): jsonRpc raised from an except branch of a try that also had a finally; under Nim 2.2.2 the exception object is lost across the finally, the error flag stays set, and the caller's typed except dereferences a nil current exception (gdb: nimBorrowCurrentException() == nil before isObjDisplayCheck). Any refused connection crashed. Fix: no finally, the client closed on each path. Minimal repro: one jsonRpc call to a closed port. rpc_budget_test and rpc_url_redaction_test pass; unit suite 139/139. Labbook: docs/labbook/nim-raise-in-except-with-finally.md.
